articles.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Chronic Liver Disease: 2026 Update.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver disease, caused by a range of etiologies, can lead to progressive liver function deterioration, hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis, and, ultimately, end-stage liver disease. With cirrhosis and end-stage liver disease, complications include portal hypertension, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, refractory ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and primary hepatocellular carcinoma. Imaging plays an important role in the diagnosis, treatment response assessment, and surveillance of chronic liver disease, specifically of hepatic hemochromatosis, steatosis, and fibrosis, in an effort to prevent progression to cirrhosis. This document reviews the imaging modalities best suited for these clinical scenarios, and a summary of current evidence is provided to support the use of various modalities for each of the clinical contexts. The American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria are evidence-based guidelines for specific clinical conditions that are reviewed annually by a multidisciplinary expert panel. The guideline development and revision include an extensive analysis of current medical literature from peer reviewed journals and the application of well-established methodologies (RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE) to rate the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios. In those instances where evidence is lacking or equivocal, expert opinion may supplement the available evidence to recommend imaging or treatment.

articles.title: Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging and 2-year Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Mild Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Background Mild hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) comprises approximately 30%-50% of neonatal encephalopathy cases, yet neurodevelopmental outcomes remain difficult to predict using clinical assessment alone. Purpose To develop and externally test a diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI)-based machine learning model for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonates with mild HIE. Materials and Methods This prospective four-hospital study consecutively enrolled neonates from November 2019 through November 2023, with 24-month follow-up completed in November 2025. The primary outcome was adverse neurodevelopment at 24 months, defined as any Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, third edition, composite score below 85; cerebral palsy; or epilepsy requiring ongoing treatment. Clinical-only, imaging-only, and combined clinical-imaging models were developed from 49 DKI parameters and seven clinical variables. Model discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and curves were compared with paired DeLong tests and false discovery rate adjustment. Results Overall, 740 neonates were included (mean gestational age, 38.3 weeks ± 1.3 [SD]; 404 [54.6%] female). Adverse outcomes occurred in 182 of 510 development cohort participants (35.7%) and 80 of 230 external test set participants (34.8%). In the external test set, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89, 0.95), with a sensitivity of 86% (69 of 80) and specificity of 85.3% (128 of 150). It exceeded the clinical-only model (AUC, 0.85; false discovery rate-adjusted P = .004) and imaging-only model (AUC, 0.86; false discovery rate-adjusted P = .005). Prespecified risk stratification yielded a negative predictive value of 100% (61 of 61) for low-risk infants and a positive predictive value of 88% (38 of 43) for high-risk infants. Conclusion In neonates with mild HIE, a combined clinical and DKI model demonstrated higher discrimination for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes than did clinical-only or imaging-only models. © The Author(s) 2026. articles.title: From detection to clinical comprehension: a cognitive hierarchy for the epistemic and ethical limits of artificial intelligence in radiology.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) detects findings in medical images at a level that, for specific tasks, matches or exceeds that of an expert radiologist. Detecting a finding, however, is not the same as understanding a disease. AI radiology literature rarely distinguishes between these two processes. This article proposes a four-level cognitive hierarchy, inspired by Ackoff's [1] model of data, information, knowledge, and wisdom, to analyze at which level current AI operates and its epistemic and ethical consequences. The four levels, detection, classification, diagnosis, and clinical comprehension, form a gradient of increasing cognitive demand. The last of these corresponds to the tacit knowledge described by Polanyi [2] and is consistent with classic studies of radiological perception. Recent literature on epistemic authority in medicine suggests that the gap between this level and AI reflects, at least in part, a difference in the type of justification underpinning clinical judgment. AI reliably automates the first two levels, makes partial progress on the third when structured clinical data are available, and currently lacks an operational counterpart for the fourth. This distinction has implications for the training of specialists and for clinical responsibility, which remains with the radiologist in AI-assisted diagnosis.

Longitudinal MR Neurography Changes and Prognostic Significance of Hourglass-like Constrictions in Parsonage-Turner Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Background Hourglass-like constrictions (HGCs) of peripheral nerves are hallmark findings of Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS), but their longitudinal characteristics and associations with motor strength and electromyography (EMG) findings, as well as their prognostic value, are unknown. Purpose To delineate longitudinal changes of HGCs and muscle edema with MR neurography (MRN) and to determine their associations with outcomes. Materials and Methods In this prospective study (July 2020 to January 2024), individuals diagnosed with PTS less than 6 months from symptom onset with EMG-confirmed muscle denervation underwent longitudinal assessments (baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months) with physical examination (for muscle strength), EMG, participant-reported outcomes, and 3-T MRN. Two readers independently counted severe and mild HGCs and graded the degree of muscle edema as "severe," "moderate," "mild," or "none." Associations of MRN findings and days from symptom onset with EMG findings and muscle strength were evaluated. Logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to assess whether baseline MRN findings were predictive of follow-up outcomes. Results Among 45 participants (median age, 47.2 years [IQR, 38.7-57.3 years]; 27 male), analyses included 58 affected nerves and 112 affected muscles. Most nerves (90% [52 of 58]) demonstrated HGCs and a median of one to two severe HGCs at baseline, which reduced in frequency (78%-82% [35-37 of 45]) and severity (zero to one) at 12 months. Muscle edema was graded moderate on average at baseline and reduced to mild at 12 months. HGCs were not associated with EMG findings or muscle strength, but a more severe muscle edema grade was associated with increased EMG denervation (odds ratio, 3.19-13.9). HGCs and muscle edema at baseline were not predictive of outcomes, except for muscle edema prediction of self-reported disability at the 3- to 6-month follow-up (β = 4.7-5.9). Conclusion HGCs persisted over the course of 1-year follow-up in PTS but were neither independently predictive of nor associated with muscle strength recovery. Muscle edema grades were associated with EMG denervation. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Evaluation of Total Patent Branch Vessel Ostial Area at Preoperative CT Angiography for Predicting Type II Endoleak after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
articles.abstract: Background Type II endoleak (T2EL) is a common complication after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) that may lead to aneurysm sac enlargement. Although guideline-based criteria are used to identify high-risk patients, their predictive accuracy remains limited. Purpose To evaluate the predictive value of preoperative total branch vessel ostial area at CT angiography (CTA) for T2EL after EVAR. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients undergoing EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) between January 2010 and December 2020. After exclusion of other endoleak types, CTA-derived anatomic parameters and outcomes were compared by isolated T2EL status. Total branch vessel ostial area was evaluated using prespecified Cox models and Cox-least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis. Discrimination and reproducibility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, intraclass correlation coefficients, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Of 216 patients in this study (mean age, 66 years ± 7.6 [SD]; 190 male; median follow-up, 4.7 years), 86 (39.8%) developed T2EL. Total branch vessel ostial area showed excellent reproducibility (intraclass correlation coefficients, 0.98-1.00) and was larger in patients with T2EL than in those without T2EL (median, 24.5 vs 11.7 mm2; P < .001). Sac enlargement was more frequent with T2EL (45.3% [39 of 86] vs 12.3% [16 of 130]; P < .001) and was associated with reintervention (hazard ratio [HR], 2.83; P = .003) but not overall survival (HR, 1.76; P = .28). In the fully adjusted Cox model, total branch vessel ostial area was associated with T2EL (HR, 1.06 per 1-mm2 increase [95% CI: 1.04, 1.08]; P < .001). Total branch ostial area showed better discrimination for T2EL than guideline-based criteria (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.82 vs 0.64; P < .001), with a Youden index-derived cutoff of 15.55 mm2. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive continuous association in T2EL risk with increasing ostial area (P < .001). Conclusion Preoperative CTA-derived total branch vessel ostial area outperformed conventional branch diameter and count criteria for predicting T2EL in patients after EVAR for infrarenal AAA. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Liddell in this issue.

articles.title: Hemorrhage Risk in Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations before and after Stereotactic Radiosurgery.
articles.abstract: Background Whether stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is associated with lower hemorrhage risk for unruptured brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) during the latency period (ie, from SRS to complete AVM obliteration) remains controversial. Purpose To evaluate whether SRS is associated with lower hemorrhage risk in unruptured brain AVMs during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included 511 patients with unruptured brain AVMs at diagnosis treated with single-session SRS between June 1990 and May 2024. Hemorrhage rates before and after SRS were calculated using the person-year method. A time-dependent Cox proportional hazards model was used to assess the association between SRS and hemorrhage risk. The pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was calculated using the interval between diagnosis and SRS. Results For the 511 patients (median age, 39 years [IQR, 28-52 years]; 306 male patients), the total observation period from diagnosis to SRS or any prior treatment was 1009 person-years, and the pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was 3.4 per 100 person-years (34 hemorrhages). Among 477 patients who underwent SRS without a pre-SRS hemorrhage, 75 patients were lost to follow-up during the latency period, and the median latency period was 33 months, with a total of 1711 person-years. Hemorrhage occurred in 24 patients during the latency period, yielding an overall latency-period hemorrhage rate of 1.4 per 100 person-years. After adjustment for age, nidus volume, and venous drainage, time-dependent Cox proportional hazards analysis showed that SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk in the post-SRS latency period compared with the pre-SRS period, corresponding to a 53% lower hazard (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47 [95% CI: 0.27, 0.83]; P = .009). SRS was also associated with lower hemorrhage risk in lesions treated with SRS following prior surgery or endovascular therapy (hazard ratio, 0.20; P = .01). Conclusion In patients with unruptured brain AVMs, SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: MoCE-GAN: Mixture of Complexity Experts with generative adversarial networks for image restoration in sparse-view and limited-view photoacoustic tomography.
articles.abstract: Photoacoustic tomography (PAT) is a hybrid imaging modality that combines optical contrast with ultrasonic penetration depth for biomedical applications. Sparse-view and limited-view sampling strategies reduce acquisition time and system complexity but introduce reconstruction artifacts that degrade image quality and clinical utility. Although deep learning methods have advanced sparse-view PAT restoration, most rely on uniform architectures that allocate a fixed computational budget to every input sample, leaving them poorly matched to the varying degradation severity across samples. We propose MoCE-GAN, which couples a Mixture-of-Complexity-Experts (MoCE) generator - selecting experts according to sample-level degradation complexity via global feature statistics and a frequency embedding - with a PatchGAN discriminator that enforces local perceptual fidelity. Experiments on embryo numerical simulation, bone numerical simulation, in vivo mouse, and in vivo human datasets evaluate sparse-view settings with 16, 32, or 64 transducers and limited-view settings with 45°, 90°, or 180° angular coverage, depending on the acquisition geometry. Compared with four representative image-domain methods (PAT-ADN, FD-UNet, SA-UNet, GAID-PAT), MoCE-GAN raises PSNR over the best baseline by an average of 1.77 dB across the 16 dataset-configuration combinations under configuration-specific training, and by 2.10 dB under mixed training, where a single model covers all configurations and yields PSNR 0.24 dB lower on average than the configuration-specific models. SSIM and LPIPS are each best in most configurations. Beyond quantitative gains, restorations remain anatomically consistent under severe undersampling, supporting accelerated or reduced-view PAT acquisition scenarios.

articles.title: Multi-center validation of DeSURVAE for meningioma tumor segmentation on contrast-enhanced MRI: robustness, domain shift, and performance confounders.
articles.abstract: Automated meningioma segmentation methods have often reported strong benchmark performance, yet real-world deployment remains constrained by domain shift across sites, heterogeneous imaging protocols, and persistent failure on small lesions. Here, we present a large-scale, multi-center validation of DeSURVAE, our BraTS 2025 winning hybrid CNN-transformer 3D-U-Net (trained from scratch), to systematically quantify robustness under clinically-realistic variability. We assembled 2317 T1-weighted contrast-enhanced MRI scans from Auckland Hospitals, BraTS 2023, and BraTS 2024 cohorts, comprising 3269 tumors. We evaluated four dataset-based training scenarios (individual, fused multi-center, cross-cohort transfer, and cross-fold transfer) using careful binarization threshold selection, lesion-wise Dice-score (DSC), and HD95 Hausdorff distance, followed by analyzing anatomical, scanner, and growth-related factors. Across scenarios, fusion training produced the strongest and most consistent performance (0.81±0.23 DSC; 29.51±79.24 mm HD95), improving overlap across cohorts (3-8 % DSC) and reducing boundary error (9-35 mm), with the largest gains in the radiotherapy cohort (BraTS 2024). Notably, DeSURVAE performed strongly on smaller lesions, achieving 0.80 DSC for pre-operative tumors as small as 0.4 cm3, a significant improvement to the literature's 2∼3 cm3 threshold. Anatomical analyses using tumor-scale-aware gridding identified tumor volume as the dominant performance driver (Spearman rs=0.57, p < 0.001), whereas coarse cortical location effects were non-significant. Scanner field strength had minimal impact, and tumor growth status was a non-significant DSC driver. Our findings highlight that careful binarization, and gridding design can uncover tumor-level performance determinants. Overall, multi-center fusion training was a key lever for clinically robust meningioma segmentation, while small lesions and radiotherapy-like domains remain priority targets for future improvements.

articles.title: Self-Supervised Uncalibrated Multi-View Video Anonymization in the Operating Room.
articles.abstract: Privacy preservation is a prerequisite for using video data in Operating Room (OR) research. Effective anonymization relies on the exhaustive localization of every individual; even a single missed detection necessitates extensive manual correction. However, existing approaches face two critical scalability bottlenecks: (1) they usually require manual annotations at each new clinical site for high accuracy; (2) multi-view approaches typically require camera calibration whenever cameras are repositioned. To address these problems, we propose a self-supervised multi-view video anonymization framework based on whole-body person detection and pose estimation, without manual annotations or camera calibration. Our core strategy is to conduct self-supervised domain adaptation of a single-view detector by "retrieving" false negatives using temporal and multi-view context. We first apply an off-the-shelf wholebody detector with a low-score threshold to gather candidate detections. Then, we retrieve low-score false negatives that are consistent with high-score detections via tracking and self-supervised, uncalibrated multi-view association. The recovered detections serve as pseudo-labels to iteratively fine-tune the detector. Finally, we apply whole-body pose estimation on each detected person, and fine-tune the pose model using its own high-score predictions. Experiments on the simulated 4D-OR dataset and our real-surgery dataset achieve 99% and 97% recall, respectively. We further train a real-time whole-body detector using the generated pseudo-labels, achieving comparable performance and highlighting our method's practical applicability. Code will be available at https://github.com/CAMMA-public/ OR_anonymization.

articles.title: MRI-guided in-bore prostate biopsy: an eight-year single-operator longitudinal experience with progressive protocol simplification and pathological validation in 1016 patients.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe the eight-year longitudinal performance of MRI-guided in-bore prostate biopsy performed by a single operator who began the study with limited dedicated in-bore experience; to evaluate the diagnostic equivalence of a simplified two-core sampling strategy compared with prior multi-core strategies after adjustment for temporal effects; and to provide pathological validation in a propensity-matched radical prostatectomy cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 1016 consecutive men with PI-RADS 3-5 lesions who underwent MRI-guided in-bore biopsy (targeted cores only, without concurrent systematic sampling) between November 2017 and November 2025. By design, all procedures were performed by one interventional radiologist on the same 1.5-T scanner (one major software upgrade in 2021), with three sequential sampling protocols (four-core, n = 185; three-core, n = 549; two-core, n = 282). Performance was assessed across five chronological quintiles. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for chronological quintile and clinical/imaging covariates. A propensity-matched radical prostatectomy cohort (n = 180) provided pathological reference. RESULTS: Overall cancer detection was 76.9% (781/1016). Across chronological quintiles, cancer detection increased from 72.9% to 78.9% (P = .04), targeting accuracy from 87.2 to 96.1% (P < .001), and procedure time decreased from 52.4 ± 9.1 to 29.7 ± 5.8 min (P < .001). After multivariable adjustment, the two-core strategy was not independently superior to multi-core strategies for clinically significant cancer detection (adjusted detection difference 4.8%, 95% CI: - 1.9% to 11.5%, P = .16), a result compatible with non-inferiority (margin 5 percentage points) rather than with superiority. In the propensity-matched surgical cohort, Gleason concordance (73-78%) and missed-cancer rates (3-5%) did not differ across strategies. Among 220 cancer-positive two-core cases, intra-biopsy Gleason concordance between central and peripheral cores was 70.0%. CONCLUSION: In this single-operator longitudinal experience, MRI-guided in-bore biopsy performance improved substantially over time. Apparent advantages of the simplified two-core strategy largely reflected accumulating operator experience rather than intrinsic sampling strategy superiority; preserved pathological accuracy supports its non-inferiority and efficiency once proficiency is achieved. CLINICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: Sequential implementation of MRI-targeted biopsy protocols can be substantially confounded by accumulating operator experience; in expert single-operator settings, a simplified two-core central-peripheral sampling strategy can match the diagnostic accuracy of multi-core approaches while reducing procedure time.

articles.title: Contrast-enhanced mammography for selecting B3 breast lesions eligible for vacuum-assisted excision: a retrospective single-centre study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Vacuum-assisted excision (VAE) has emerged as an alternative to surgical excision for B3 lesions, although lesions upgraded to malignancy at VAE still require surgery. This study aimed to determine whether contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) can distinguish B3 lesions eligible for VAE at lower risk of upgrade from those at higher risk. METHODS: A retrospective, single-centre study was conducted on B3 lesions diagnosed from January 2019 to December 2024 at our institution. B3 lesions diagnosed at core needle or vacuum-assisted biopsy, deemed eligible for VAE by the multidisciplinary team and examined with CEM before VAE were included. The primary outcome was the per-lesion diagnostic performance of CEM in identifying B3 lesions eligible for VAE at increased risk of upgrading, using VAE histology as the reference standard. Secondary, exploratory outcomes included the diagnostic performance of CEM across different patient subgroups and lesion types. RESULTS: Of 884 B3 lesions diagnosed during the study period, 292 lesions in 283 patients (nine with bilateral lesions) were included. VAE was performed under digital breast tomosynthesis guidance in 228/292 (78.1%) lesions and under ultrasound guidance in 64/292 (21.9%). Twenty of 292 (6.8%) lesions were upgraded to malignancy at VAE. CEM had a sensitivity of 75.0% (95% CI 50.9-91.3%), specificity of 96.0% (92.9-98.0%), positive predictive value (PPV) of 57.7% (36.9-76.6%) and negative predictive value (NPV) of 98.1% (95.7-99.4%) in predicting upgrade, with an accuracy of 94.5% (91.3-96.8%); the AUC was 0.855. CONCLUSIONS: B3 lesions without enhancement on CEM have a low probability of malignant upgrade. The high NPV of CEM could increase confidence in VAE as a definitive treatment and help optimise the selection of patients with B3 lesions eligible for VAE.

articles.title: Enhancing brain metastasis detection on contrast-enhanced CT: the impact of maximum intensity projection (MIP) among radiologists with different levels of expertise.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Brain metastases are the most common intracranial tumors in adults, pivotal for staging/treatment. Although MRI is the gold standard, contrast-enhanced brain CT is frequently used during oncologic follow-up, often interpreted by general radiologists. Maximum intensity projection (MIP) is a CT post-processing technique widely used in thoracic and vascular imaging but underexplored in neuro-oncology. We evaluated whether CT-MIP improves lesion detection according to reader expertise, metastatic burden, and lesion size. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective single-center study of 98 patients who underwent brain MRI within 30 days of contrast-enhanced whole-body CT. Four readers (two general radiologists, two neuroradiologists) reviewed CT examinations using conventional images and CT-MIP (7-mm slabs). Primary endpoint was lesion count. Subgroup analyses were performed according to metastatic burden (oligometastatic disease) and lesion size ( < 5 mm). Secondary endpoints included interpretation time and lesion size assessment. RESULTS: Overall, MRI yielded higher lesion counts than conventional CT and CT-MIP (both p < 0.001). CT-MIP significantly increased lesion counts compared with CT for all readers (p  <  0.05). In oligometastatic patients, CT-MIP showed a smaller discrepancy from MRI for general radiologists than in higher-burden cases (p < 0.001), yielding results comparable to neuroradiologists using conventional CT. CT-MIP significantly improved detection in patients with at least one metastasis < 5 mm, regardless of expertise, and reduced interpretation time. CONCLUSION: CT-MIP improves CT-based detection of brain metastases, particularly among less-experienced readers, reducing the performance gap with neuroradiologists and providing lesion counts closer to MRI in oligometastatic disease and small metastases. While MRI remains the reference standard, CT-MIP is a simple, cost-free adjunct when MRI is unavailable or delayed.

articles.title: Emergency uterine arteries embolization for severe post-partum hemorrhage: a two-center retrospective analysis on reproductive outcomes, psychological impact and clinical efficacy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Emergency uterine arteries embolization (E-UAE) is an established uterus-sparing treatment for severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) refractory to conservative management. We evaluated the effects of E-UAE for severe PPH on ovarian cycle, reproductive outcomes and patient-reported psychological outcomes, and its clinical efficacy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-center observational study included consecutive patients who underwent E-UAE for severe PPH between July 2020 and December 2024 and completed a structured telephone questionnaire by December 31, 2025. The questionnaire assessed menstrual cycle recovery, regularity and flow, subsequent pregnancies and outcomes, desire for further pregnancy, and fear of future pregnancy using a numeric rating scale. Clinical and procedural outcomes were retrieved from medical records. Embolic-material analyses were exploratory and hypothesis-generating. RESULTS: Thirty-three patients completed the questionnaire after a median follow-up of 42 months (IQR, 17 months). E-UAE avoided hysterectomy in 29/33 patients (87.9%), none requiring re-embolization. Among women with uterine preservation, ovarian cycle resumed in 28/29 (96.6%), and 27/28 (96.4%) reported regular menses. Fourteen women desired further pregnancy, of whom 11/14 (78.6%) achieved at least one pregnancy; 14 pregnancies included 10 term deliveries, 2 miscarriages, and 2 ectopic pregnancies. Fear of recurrent PPH was the most frequent reason for avoiding further pregnancies. Comparisons by embolic material efficacy showed no statistically significant differences (p = 0.62). CONCLUSION: E-UAE is an effective uterus-sparing treatment for severe PPH, associated with high menstrual recovery and subsequent pregnancy among women attempting conception. Fear of recurrent PPH was the most frequently reported reason for not pursuing a subsequent pregnancy and should be addressed during follow-up.

articles.title: Quantitative pulmonary [¹⁸F]FMISO uptake in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in a prospective proof-of-concept PET/CT study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disease with variable clinical trajectories and treatment responses. CT depicts structural abnormalities but may not identify biologically abnormal lung. We evaluated pulmonary uptake of the hypoxia-sensitive tracer [¹⁸F]fluoromisonidazole ([¹⁸F]FMISO) in IPF and its cross-sectional associations with CT measurements and pulmonary function. METHODS: In this prospective proof-of-concept study with cross-sectional analyses, 10 participants with IPF and 10 age-matched healthy controls underwent [¹⁸F]FMISO PET/CT at 2 h and 4 h after injection. Whole-lung and CT-defined regional mean standardized uptake values (SUVmean) were measured. Post hoc sensitivity analyses were applied using CT-derived non-air-fraction correction to whole-lung SUVmean and to compartments below ​-400 HU and below ​-700 HU in both groups. Group comparisons accounted for independent and paired measurements. Pearson or Spearman coefficients correlations were used. Holm adjustment was applied within defined comparison families. RESULTS: Twenty male participants were included. At 4 h, uncorrected whole-lung SUVmean was higher in IPF than in healthy controls (0.521 ± 0.114 vs. 0.344 ± 0.050, adjusted p = 0.0028). After non-air-fraction correction, the difference persisted (mean difference: 0.158, pointwise 95% CI: 0.074-0.242, adjusted p = 0.0042). Corrected regional SUVmean at 4 h was also higher in IPF below -400 HU (1.721 ± 0.251 vs. 1.375 ± 0.220, adjusted p = 0.0215), with a consistent finding below ​-700 HU (adjusted p = 0.0054). Corrected mean comparisons at 2 h were non-significant with Welch's t tests. Within IPF, uncorrected whole-lung SUVmean at 4 h strongly correlated with mean lung attenuation (r = 0.812, adjusted p = 0.0172) and percent-predicted TLC (r = -0.794, adjusted p = 0.0244). CONCLUSION: Higher [¹⁸F]FMISO uptake in IPF persisted at 4 h after estimated non-air-fraction correction in whole-lung and lower-attenuation regional measurements. Longitudinal validation of this potential imaging biomarker as a surrogate of hypoxia-specific trapping is required. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05331729. articles.title: Multimodal PET/MR imaging in Alzheimer's disease: A comparative study of structural, metabolic, synaptic and perfusion measures.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Structural MRI and 18F-FDG PET are clinically established imaging biomarkers of neuronal injury in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Synaptic density PET (SV2A), arterial spin labelling (ASL, perfusion), and cortical thickness (CTh) can offer additional information, but have not been compared within the same patients. We performed a head-to-head evaluation of these imaging measures for detecting neurodegeneration, discriminating AD from healthy volunteers (HV) and examining their associations with cognition. METHODS: Thirty-six biomarker-confirmed AD patients (71 ± 9 y/o; M/F 17/19) underwent 18F-FDG, 18F-SynVesT-1 PET/MR and neuropsychological evaluation. Patients were classified as MCI-stage (CDR = 0.5, n = 22) or dementia-stage (CDR > 0.5, n = 14). Image processing and analysis was performed in CAT12.9 with partial volume correction for PET. PET and ASL measures were normalized to the whole cerebellum. Classification performance was evaluated with partial least squares discriminant analysis and Firth logistic regression under repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation. RESULTS: In the MCI-stage, reductions were mainly found in the temporal cortex. In the dementia-stage, reductions for the 5 imaging measures extended to the temporoparietal, precuneal and frontal cortices. 18F-FDG PET, assessed against a separate HV cohort, showed large reductions (Cohen's d up to -2.5) and excellent discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.94). Among the cortical measures evaluated against the same HV, cortical thickness showed the largest reductions (d up to -1.6). Cortical thickness, 18F-SynVesT-1 and volumetry provided similar discriminatory performance (AUC 0.81-0.86). ASL did not show detectable reductions in MCI and had a lower AUC (0.72). Global cognition was associated with widespread atrophy, cortical thinning, and 18F-FDG hypometabolism, whereas domain-specific cognitive measures showed more localized regional associations. 18F-SynVesT-1 and ASL demonstrated weaker and less consistent correlations. CONCLUSION: Multimodal PET and MRI measures showed overlapping yet distinct spatial patterns of neurodegeneration. In MCI, structural, metabolic and synaptic abnormalities were found, whereas perfusion deficits only significantly emerged in dementia-stage AD. Structural and functional measures differentially relate to global and domain-specific cognitive decline. The study was registered on clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05384353) as of 20 May 2022.

articles.title: Proposed quantitative workflow for localization and characterization of parathyroid adenoma using dual-energy 4D CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To construct an imaging workflow using 4D DECT for the localization and characterization of parathyroid adenomas. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This IRB-approved, HIPAA-compliant retrospective study included patients who underwent DECT of the neck between June 1, 2023, and May 30, 2024, with pathology-confirmed parathyroid adenomas. A research fellow with 12 years of clinical radiology experience obtained attenuation of parathyroid adenoma, thyroid, lymph node on non-contrast, virtual non-contrast, 70 keV and 55 keV dual-energy CT, and iodine maps for arterial and venous phases. Two additional clinical fellows repeated the measurements to evaluate the interobserver variability. Conspicuity of the lesion was calculated by contrast-to-noise ratio of the parathyroid relative to the thyroid gland. Statistical analysis employed the Friedman test, Mann-Whitney U tests, one-way ANOVA, and ROC curves. RESULTS: The study included 40 patients (31 females; mean age 57.7 ± 13.4 years) with 55 confirmed parathyroid adenomas. The highest contrast-to-noise ratio was seen in arterial-phase iodine concentration (5.7; IQR: 3.5-9.6). Non-contrast (AUC: 0.91), using cutoff value < 54 HU, achieved 81.8 (71.8-91.8)% sensitivity and 95 (88.6-100)% specificity for differentiation of parathyroid from thyroid, and 55 keV arterial (AUC: 0.97), using cutoff value of > 150 HU on 55 keV arterial phase achieved 94.5 (88.4-100) % sensitivity and 90 (80.8-99.2) % specificity for differentiation of parathyroid from lymph node. Combining cutoff values and within-patient pairwise comparison between the lesion, thyroid, and lymph node increased sensitivity to 98% for the characterization of parathyroid adenoma. CONCLUSION: Workflow strategy using a combination of cutoff and within-patient pairwise analysis on non-contrast, 55 keV arterial and venous-phase DECT achieved high sensitivity for detection and characterization of parathyroid adenoma. KEY POINTS: Question What is a systematic imaging approach for image review and measurement for identification and characterization of parathyroid adenoma on multiphasic dual-energy CT? Findings A systematic workflow combining arterial-phase iodine mapping, non-contrast, 55 keV arterial threshold cutoffs, and within-patient pairwise analysis achieved 98.2% sensitivity for parathyroid adenoma. Clinical relevance The proposed quantitative workflow for the identification and characterization of parathyroid adenoma in multiphasic dual-energy CT may enhance preoperative localization of suspected parathyroid adenomas. Its effects on surgical approach, procedure time, cost, and morbidity require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: A survey across 200 European institutions on intracranial and extracranial carotid MR-vessel wall imaging practice.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: We aimed to capture the current practice of intracranial and extracranial carotid Vessel Wall Imaging (VWI) across European institutions, and to identify practical, technical or educational obstacles to its successful implementation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An online survey on the use of VWI, endorsed by European Society of Neuroradiology (ESNR) in collaboration with American Society of Neuroradiology (ASNR) was performed between April and July 2023. The survey was anonymous and distributed via e-mail to ESNR members and associated National Societies. Only one member per institution could respond. Response data are summarized as frequencies and percentages. RESULTS: There were 200 valid institutional respondents. The majority (84%) were neuroradiologists; 67.5% came from an academic hospital. Most respondents relied on vendor assistance for technical protocol development. Overall, 33% practiced only intracranial VWI, whereas 3% only extracranial; the majority (48.5%) did both. Both intracranial and extracranial-VWI were most commonly performed on average 1-2 times per month and for clinical use. Main intracranial and extracranial VWI indications were differentiation of vasculopathies (97.5%) and characterization/detection of dissection (76.5%), respectively. Interestingly, only 62.5% of intracranial VWI-users applied sequences with specific blood-flow suppression. A large proportion of intracranial (77.3%) and extra-cranial (72.4%) VWI-users indicated an interest in learning more about the technique. CONCLUSION: VWI is regularly practiced on a clinical ground across European institutions, particularly in academic hospitals; however, the results of this survey stress the need for further education and harmonization to promote VWI successful use. KEY POINTS: Question We explored the current state of VWI practice in Europe focusing on indications, frequency of use, adherence to technical recommendations and confidence in interpretation. Findings Our survey highlights VWI is often applied without appropriate technical requirements; users frequently express lack of confidence regarding technical aspects and interpretation of VWI studies. Clinical relevance Real-life data from VWI practice in Europe highlight important shortcomings (potentially causing clinical misdiagnosis of vessel-wall pathology), which need to be addressed with further education and call for a more widespread network of technical and clinical support.

articles.title: Symptomatic minor instability of the lateral elbow: applicability of the SMILE concept to magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Symptomatic minor instability of the lateral elbow (SMILE) has recently emerged as an explanation for atraumatic lateral elbow pain and has previously been described using arthroscopy and CT arthrography. This study evaluated the reader-detected frequency and reproducibility of MRI findings associated with the SMILE concept and investigated its applicability to routine elbow MRI. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, consecutive atraumatic elbow MRI examinations performed between January 2020 and May 2024 were independently evaluated by three readers. MRI findings associated with the SMILE concept were assessed together with extra-articular abnormalities of static and dynamic stabilizers. Agreement for individual MRI findings was assessed using Fleiss' κ, while agreement for the MRI-based SMILE sum score was evaluated using pairwise quadratically weighted Cohen's κ and a three-reader intraclass correlation coefficient. RESULTS: Elbow MRI examinations from 122 patients with atraumatic lateral elbow pain were included (mean age 48.0 ± 14.1 years; 68 men). The MRI-based SMILE sum score demonstrated substantial-to-almost perfect pairwise agreement (weighted κ = 0.674-0.861) with good overall three-reader agreement (ICC = 0.772). Among the individual SMILE items, humeroradial asymmetry demonstrated the highest reproducibility, whereas trochlear ridge chondromalacia showed the lowest. Extra-articular abnormalities demonstrated substantial-to-almost perfect agreement, particularly epicondylitis and lateral ligament abnormalities. CONCLUSION: MRI enables reproducible assessment of instability-associated abnormalities in patients with atraumatic lateral elbow pain, supporting the feasibility of an MRI-based SMILE concept in clinical routine. Besides intra-articular findings, MRI reproducibly depicts extra-articular pathologies, thereby broadening the imaging assessment of lateral elbow pain. KEY POINTS: Question Can MRI reproducibly assess SMILE-associated abnormalities in atraumatic elbows? Findings MRI-based evaluation of SMILE-associated abnormalities and extra-articular stabilizer pathologies was highly reproducible across three readers. Clinical relevance MRI allows reproducible assessment of SMILE-associated and extra-articular abnormalities in atraumatic lateral elbow pain and may broaden the imaging assessment beyond CT arthrography.

articles.title: A Retrospective study of ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT for predicting immunochemotherapy response and differentiating tumor residue in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the predictive and diagnostic value of baseline and post-treatment 18F-FDG PET/CT metabolic and structural features in distinguishing true residual tumor from immune-related inflammation in LA-NPC. METHODS: This single-center retrospective analysis enrolled 95 consecutive stage III-IVA LA-NPC patients receiving first-line neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. All underwent pre- and post-treatment 18F-FDG PET/CT measuring metabolic parameters and structural features (extranodal extension [ENE]). Depth of metabolic response (DMR) was the primary endpoint; biopsy histopathology (n = 22) acted as gold standard. Multivariable regression, Spearman correlation, ROC-AUC with bootstrap validation, and sensitivity analyses were applied. RESULTS: Baseline SUVmax (OR = 1.146 [95% CI: 1.051, 1.250]; P = 0.002) and ENE (OR = 0.171 [95% CI: 0.054, 0.544]; P = 0.003) independently predicted poor and strong DMR, respectively. Patients with baseline ENE showed higher post-treatment EBV DNA non-clearance rates (34.1% vs. 9.8%; P = 0.008). In the biopsy subgroup with discordant biochemical-imaging status, true residue had higher baseline primary tumor TLG (P = 0.048) and ENE prevalence (80.0% vs. 16.7%; P = 0.028) than inflammation. A post-treatment nodal-dominant pattern (Post-T/N ratio ≤ 0.9) was associated with a lower rate of pathologically confirmed primary-tumour residue than a primary-dominant pattern (11.1% vs. 46.2%), negatively correlating with peak CRP (rho = -0.523, P = 0.012), indicating that nodal-dominant uptake accompanied a more intense systemic inflammatory response rather than residual disease. CONCLUSION: In LA-NPC, baseline SUVmax and ENE independently predict neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy response. Combining baseline metabolic and nodal structural features distinguishes true residual disease from immune-related inflammation.

articles.title: Longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET changes map onto distinct cholinergic and serotonergic territories in autoimmune encephalitis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) shows a longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET signature: acute hypermetabolism in limbic-striatal-thalamic regions and hypometabolism in posterior associative cortex, both partially reversible under immunotherapy. Whether these patterns show spatial correspondence with specific neuromodulatory systems is unknown. METHODS: This retrospective secondary analysis included twenty-two AE patients from a previously published longitudinal cohort (Cerne et al. 2025) who underwent [¹⁸F]FDG PET at clinical baseline (BS) and follow-up (FU). Using JuSpace (option 6), atlas-regional BS-FU difference maps were correlated (Spearman) with 15 normative PET/SPECT maps of multiple neurotransmitter systems. Participant-level Spearman coefficients were Fisher-z transformed. Group inference used paired BS/FU label permutations, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across all 15 maps. Spatial co-localization was interpreted as overlap in regional involvement, not as directionality of transmitter signaling. Age-adjusted regression models tested associations between individual JuSpace coefficients and clinical outcomes at BS and FU. RESULTS: Longitudinal metabolic change showed positive spatial associations with VAChT (Fisher z = 0.164; ρ = 0.185; q = 0.023) and α4β2 (z = 0.133; ρ = 0.127; q = 0.004), and a negative association with 5-HT2A (z = - 0.108; ρ=-0.093; q = 0.014). The cholinergic alignment matches the previously described hypermetabolic limbic-striatal circuit, whereas the 5-HT2A alignment situates reversible posterior hypometabolism within serotonin-enriched association cortex. No exploratory clinical association survived multiplicity correction. CONCLUSION: Longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET differences showed significant spatial correspondence with distinct neuromodulatory territories. Embedding longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET changes into a normative receptor space provides a systems-level neurochemical framework and generates testable hypotheses on how cholinergic subcortico-limbic and 5-HT2A-enriched posterior association territories relate to acute disease expression and recovery.

articles.title: Case 352: Collision Tumor of Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor and Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.
articles.abstract: A 76-year-old woman presented with a 6-month history of progressive anorexia, unintentional weight loss, and heartburn. She reported no abdominal pain, vomiting, gastrointestinal bleeding, or fever but reported intermittent bilateral lower-extremity edema. Physical examination revealed a relatively firm abdominal wall with a palpable upper abdominal mass and no peritoneal signs. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated normocytic anemia (hemoglobin level, 91 g/L; reference range, 115-150 g/L), mild thrombocytosis, no leukocytosis (white blood cell count, 6.24 × 109/L; reference range, 3.5 × 109/L to 9.5 × 109/L), severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin level, 19.5 g/L; reference range, 40.0-55.0 g/L) with low total protein, and electrolyte abnormalities including hyponatremia (sodium level, 128.4 mmol/L; reference range, 137-147 mmol/L) and hypocalcemia (total calcium level, 1.80-1.92 mmol/L; reference range, 2.11-2.52 mmol/L). The D-dimer level was markedly elevated (4900 µg/L [26.8 nmol/L]; reference range, <500 μg/L [<2.7 nmol/L]), whereas serum creatinine level was within the reference range, and serum tumor markers (α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9) were not elevated. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis and fluorine 18 (18F) fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT were performed.

articles.abstract: History A 31-year-old female patient with past medical history of uterine leiomyomas, hypertension, and migraines underwent CT for evaluation of an abdominal wall hernia, and lesions were incidentally discovered (Fig 1). Evaluation Design and Reported Accuracy of Deep Learning Mandibular Canal Segmentation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Reported accuracy of deep learning mandibular canal segmentation varies widely, and studies differ in how it was evaluated. This systematic review estimated accuracy under explicit validity criteria and described how it varied with evaluation design. Five databases were searched to May 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261403406). Dice similarity coefficients (DSCs) from three-dimensional, patient-level-partitioned cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) or CT test sets were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis on the logit scale. Public benchmark results were analyzed separately, and test sets whose reference was generated by the evaluated model were not pooled. Fifty-four studies were included. Pooled DSC across 15 studies was 0.826 (95% confidence interval 0.752-0.881; 95% prediction interval 0.444-0.966), close to three previous reviews with different inclusion rules (0.80-0.84). The 16 CBCT studies ineligible for pooling, mostly for two-dimensional slice-level segmentation or fewer than 10 test patients, reported a higher median DSC (0.860 versus 0.803). Two systems on the official ToothFairy test set had a pooled DSC of 0.751. Internal and external estimates did not differ significantly (P =  .974), but five external studies cannot establish equivalence. Pooled 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance across seven studies was 1.15 mm, with a prediction interval extending to 6.11 mm. Risk of bias was unclear or high in 14 of 15 pooled studies, and certainty of evidence was very low. Average accuracy is consistent across reviews, higher median values came, descriptively, from less constrained evaluations, and external evidence is too limited to show that performance transfers to new settings. Expert verification and prospective external validation remain necessary.

SSR AI committee position statement: top 10 high-impact AI applications and value propositions for musculoskeletal radiologists.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Effective application of artificial intelligence (AI) in musculoskeletal (MSK) radiology depends on targeting unmet clinical needs rather than technical feasibility. This Society of Skeletal Radiology (SSR) position statement identifies and prioritizes the most impactful AI applications and value propositions for MSK radiologists. METHODS: The SSR AI Committee (n = 18) used structured brainstorming to compile lists of AI-based applications and value propositions. After deduplication, standardization, and categorization using a 12-component MSK radiology value cycle, refined lists were distributed as electronic surveys to 122 SSR committee members; 103 (84.4%) and 102 (83.6%) completed the applications and value propositions surveys, respectively, scoring each item on a 5-point Likert scale. Top 10 lists were generated from summed scores. RESULTS: Brainstorming generated 208 AI application and 126 value proposition ideas, condensed to 138 and 56 unique items, respectively. Fourteen AI applications and 13 value propositions shared the top 10 ranks (tied scores). Top-ranked AI applications were within dictation and reporting (5 items), archiving and presentation (2), diagnostic imaging (1), follow-up imaging (2), quality/safety (2), and protocoling (2). Top-ranked value propositions were within dictation and reporting (4), diagnostic imaging (3), ordering (3), protocoling (2), and quality/safety (1). The highest-ranked application was AI-assisted comparison study retrieval (mean 3.17/4.0) and the highest-ranked value proposition was increased reporting efficiency (mean 3.30/4.0). CONCLUSIONS: This position statement provides a demand-driven roadmap for AI development in MSK radiology. Workflow and reporting tools were prioritized over disease detection algorithms, highlighting a gap between clinical needs and current commercial AI offerings.

articles.title: A closer look at magnetic field corrections for a 0.35 T MRI-Linac.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Magnetic FIeld COrrection (FICO) was implemented on a 0.35 T MRI-Linac to minimize B0 off-resonances. FICO parameters were derived from phantom measurements conducted at 30° gantry angle increments. FICO data were interpolated for every gantry angle, stored in a look-up table, and read during MRI-Linac simulation and treatment. PURPOSE: Verify the performance and efficacy of FICO. METHODS: We measured off-resonances in a 24 cm diameter spherical volume phantom and compared the FICO values to our measurements conducted at every: (1) gantry angle for center frequency and gradient shim; (2) 2° increment for B0 eddy currents; and (3) 10° increment for gradient and cross-term eddy currents. FICO results were compared with pre-FICO methods using the settings from a single home gantry angle (HGA), for example, 300°. RESULTS: Off-resonances decreased from a mean of -20.19 (HGA) to -0.61 Hz (FICO). Dispersion decreased from 81.10 Hz (HGA) to 52.71 Hz (FICO) and 28.0 Hz (FICO with gradient shim updates). B0 eddy currents remained within specification (± 0.1 µT∙m/mT) with FICO. X-B0 and Y-B0 eddy currents exceeded the limit when using HGA. Gradient and cross-term eddy currents were within limits (± 0.1%) for both FICO and HGA. X and cross-term (Y→X, and X→Z) eddy currents were significantly smaller with FICO than with HGA (p ≤ 0.02). Gradient eddy currents generally dropped by 24% using FICO versus HGA. X and Y gradient shim root mean square errors dropped by half by reducing the gantry angle increment from 30° to 20°. CONCLUSIONS: FICO resulted in reductions in center frequency offsets and full width at half maximum (FWHM) values, gradient shim amplitudes, and B0 eddy currents. Therefore, FICO is beneficial for minimizing off-resonances. However, FICO will benefit from using smaller gantry angle increments for interpolations and updating the gradient shim amplitudes and center frequency offsets before each treatment gantry angle.

articles.title: A multi-resolution SWIN transformer framework regularized by white matter time-intensity curve for brain dynamic contrast-enhanced MR image registration.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep learning-based registration methods are often computationally intensive and struggle with dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) images, as they cannot effectively distinguish motion artifacts from contrast-induced intensity variations, leading to unreliable physiological parameter estimation. PURPOSE: To develop a novel registration framework (TIC-SViT) based on a multi-resolution SWIN transformer architecture that exploits the inherent smoothness of tissue time-intensity curves (TICs). METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on DCE-MRI brain data from 59 subjects, acquired using a 3.0 T scanner with a T1-weighted spoiled gradient echo sequence. The dataset was randomly split into training (n = 4956), validation (n = 1180), and testing (n = 59) pairs. Model performance was assessed in terms of computational efficiency, registration accuracy, and clinical relevance. Comparative experiments were conducted against four representative registration approaches: the traditional optimization-based method ANTs, a CNN-based deep learning model, the groupwise multi-resolution framework (GWMS), and the transformer-based C2FViT framework. Computational efficiency was assessed by comparing parameter count, training time, and testing time per DCE-MRI case. Registration accuracy was quantified using Dice coefficient (DC) and the 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) across white matter, gray matter, and cerebrospinal fluid. In addition, the temporal smoothness of TICs in arterial, venous, and white matter regions was evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE). Clinical relevance was examined by comparing the quality of DCE-derived parameter maps generated from different registration methods. RESULTS: The proposed TIC-SViT model achieved a comparable parameter count (12.2 M, compared with 11.7, 9.5, and 12.4 M for CNN, GWMS, and C2FViT, respectively), the shortest training time and competitive testing speed (775 s and 11.7 s per case, compared with 1142 and 52.6 s for CNN, 1440 and 8.9 s for GWMS, 857 and 39.4 s for C2FViT, and 159.3 s for ANTs, which does not require training). It also produced the lowest RMSE values for TICs in artery (0.12), venous (0.14), and white matter (0.15) regions among all compared methods. In terms of global registration accuracy, C2FViT achieved the best performance, with DC values of 0.98, 0.97, and 0.82 for white matter, gray matter and cerebrospinal fluid, respectively, and the lowest HD95 value (9.5). The proposed TIC-SViT achieved the second best performance, with DC values of 0.97, 0.96, and 0.81, and HD95 of 10.2. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed method demonstrated registration accuracy comparable to that of state-of-the-art methods, but with significant improvement in computational efficiency.

articles.title: Impacts of Retrospective Lipid Suppression on Metabolite Quantification in Preclinical Proton MR Spectroscopic Imaging.
articles.abstract: Extracranial lipid contamination remains a challenge in proton magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (MRSI), especially in short acquisition delay MRSI, where broad lipid resonances overlap with metabolite and macromolecular signals. Although retrospective lipid suppression techniques are widely used in human MRSI, their effects on metabolite quantification in preclinical MRSI, which is more prone to lipid contamination, have not yet been examined. In this study, we assessed how the retrospective lipid suppression and spectral fitting range influence spectral quality, spatial metabolite mapping, and quantification variability using proton MRSI of rat brains at 14.1 T. Lipid suppression was applied via an orthogonal projection method to both fully sampled and compressed sensing datasets, each comprising data with minimal and pronounced lipid contamination. Spectral fitting was performed with both broad (4.1-0.2 ppm) and narrow (4.1-1.8 ppm) ranges. When lipid contamination was minimal, suppression caused only slight spectral and spatial changes, with consistent metabolite quantification across conditions. In contrast, datasets with pronounced lipid contamination exhibited notable spectral changes following suppression, consequently affecting spatial metabolite mapping and concentration estimates. Group analysis revealed that metabolites with low concentration estimates were most affected. Similar effects were observed in compressed sensing datasets. Our results provide a better understanding of the impact of retrospective lipid suppression on metabolite quantification in preclinical MRSI, thereby supporting future optimizations for its effective application.

articles.title: High-Resolution 3D UTE MRI for Integrated Radiation-Free Pulmonary and Osseous Thoracic Imaging.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study is to propose a three-dimensional ultrashort echo time (3D UTE) MRI technique for integrated, radiation-free thoracic imaging and evaluate its performance for simultaneous visualization of pulmonary and osseous thoracic structures. Five volunteers were scanned on a clinical 3-T MRI system using respiratory-gated 3D UTE and zero echo time (ZTE) sequences. UTE and ZTE were compared at matched 1.6-mm isotropic resolution to assess image quality. UTE acquisitions were further performed at isotropic resolutions of 1.6, 1.4, and 1.2 mm to determine the optimal balance between spatial resolution and clinically feasible scan time. The effects of respiratory gating were evaluated by comparing gated and free-breathing acquisitions. Contrast inversion and multistructure segmentation were applied to generate CT-like bone images and 3D renderings of the lungs, rib cage, and spine. Compared with ZTE, UTE provided more homogeneous signal intensity; reduced excitation-related artifacts; and improved delineation of pulmonary vasculature, airways, and vertebral cortical bone. Increasing spatial resolution progressively improved visualization of fine pulmonary and osseous structures, with 1.2-mm isotropic resolution yielding the highest image quality while maintaining a clinically acceptable scan time of ~7 min. Respiratory gating further improved image sharpness by reducing motion-related blurring, particularly in the lungs. The optimized UTE acquisition enabled simultaneous high-resolution visualization of lung parenchyma, ribs, and spine and supported successful 3D segmentation and rendering of multiple thoracic structures from a single dataset. The proposed 3D UTE MRI enables high-resolution, simultaneous imaging of pulmonary and osseous thoracic anatomy within a single radiation-free examination. Compared with ZTE, UTE demonstrated superior image quality and structural delineation, supporting its potential as a comprehensive alternative to CT for integrated thoracic assessment.

articles.title: EffNetV2M-ViT: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for MRI-Based Differentiation of Glioblastoma and Brain Metastasis.
articles.abstract: Noninvasive differentiation between glioblastoma (GBM) and brain metastasis (BM) remains challenging because of substantial overlap in their MRI appearance. Existing deep learning (DL) approaches have primarily relied on either convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which capture local spatial features, or transformer-based models, which capture long-range contextual relationships. However, the complementary value of combining these representations for GBM-BM discrimination has not been sufficiently investigated, using independently validated multicenter data. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer (ViT) framework for automated differentiation of GBM from BM. The framework integrates EfficientNet-based convolutional feature extraction with ViT-based global feature modeling through parallel fusion. Enhancing tumor was automatically segmented using 3D U-Net, with segmentations visually reviewed and manually corrected when necessary. T2-weighted (T2W) and contrast enhanced T1-weighted (CE-T1W) MRI sequences were used as inputs. A modality ablation study was performed to identify the optimal contrast combination among T1W, CE-T1W, T2W, and FLAIR. The framework was evaluated in a retrospective cohort of 344 patients with histologically confirmed tumors using cross-validation and ensemble methods, with performance further assessed in an independent multicenter external validation cohort from different institutions, MRI scanner platforms, and patient populations. The hybrid EffNetV2M-ViT framework achieved an accuracy of 95.4%, F1-score of 96.2%, and AUC of 98.4% on the internal test set, and 90.9%, 92.7%, and 96.8% on external validation, with sensitivity, specificity of 96.2%, 93.9% and 90.5%, 91.7%, respectively. The hybrid model outperformed the standalone CNN and ViT models across both datasets, with the largest performance gains observed in the external validation cohort, support its generalizability. Ablation analysis confirmed that the paired CE-T1W + T2W input yielded the most consistent performance across both cohorts, with additional contrasts providing no added benefit. These findings suggest that combining local convolutional features with global contextual representations improves automated GBM-BM discrimination, offering a noninvasive, standardized approach for MRI-based tumor classification that may support clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Improving Oxygen Extraction Fraction (OEF) Mapping From Integrated Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping and Quantitative Blood Oxygen Level Dependent Imaging (QSM+qBOLD, or QQ) by Learning Temporal Signal Evolution.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To improve deep learning-based QSM+qBOLD (QQ) oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) mapping by explicitly learning the temporal evolution of the multi-echo gradient-echo (mGRE) magnitude signal, whose decay encodes the tissue oxygenation that QQ-based OEF mapping depends on. METHODS: 3D multi-echo gradient echo images were acquired in 34 ischemic stroke patients with arterial spin labeling (ASL) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). We developed QQ-S, a deep learning method that estimates OEF by inverting the QQ model. QQ-S extends QQ-NET by adding convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) modules to the encoder to process the mGRE echoes sequentially. To isolate the effect of this architectural change, both networks were trained with the same simulated data and training scheme including the loss function. OEF maps from QQ-S and QQ-NET were compared in simulation and ischemic stroke patients. RESULTS: In simulation, QQ-S provided more accurate OEF than QQ-NET, with lower mean absolute error (MAE) against the simulation ground truth: 3.43% vs. 5.03% in normal-appearing tissue and 4.88% vs. 10.60% in low-OEF lesions. In subacute stroke patients, where no ground truth is available, the lesion-to-contralateral OEF ratio was significantly lower with QQ-S than with QQ-NET (0.71 ± 0.26 vs. 0.81 ± 0.24; p < 0.001), suggesting more sensitive detection of lesion OEF, consistent with PET reports in the subacute phase. OEF in acute lesions and normal-appearing tissue was comparable between methods. CONCLUSION: By explicitly learning inter-echo signal evolution with ConvLSTM, QQ-S improves OEF accuracy over QQ-NET, offering a promising tool for assessing tissue viability from conventional mGRE data.

articles.title: A prospective comparison of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 and [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT for evaluating viable brain metastases in lung cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Standard [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT has suboptimal sensitivity for assessing viable brain metastases due to high physiological brain background. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted PET, with minimal brain expression, may overcome this limitation. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 versus [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT for detecting viable brain metastases in lung cancer and evaluate their complementary value. METHODS: In this prospective intra-individual study, 24 lung cancer patients with brain metastases underwent both [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 and [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT within 3 days. Images were independently and blindly reviewed by two senior nuclear medicine physicians. Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy) was evaluated per-lesion and per-patient against a composite reference standard (characteristic imaging features, ≥ 3-month follow-up, comprehensive clinical evaluation). Quantitative parameters (SUVmax, target-to-background ratio [TBR], background uptake [SUVbgd]) and complementary detection patterns were analyzed. RESULTS: Among 43 lesions (36 viable, 7 non-viable), [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 demonstrated significantly higher per-lesion sensitivity (83.3% vs. 75.0%, P = 0.032) and accuracy (86.0% vs. 79.1%, P = 0.002) than [¹⁸F]FDG. Per-patient sensitivity (89.5% vs. 73.7%, P = 0.004) and accuracy (91.7% vs. 79.2%, P = 0.003) were also superior. The AUC for [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 was 0.917 (95% CI: 0.834-0.999) versus 0.875 (95% CI: 0.772-0.978) for [¹⁸F]FDG (P = 0.031). [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 provided dramatically higher TBR in viable lesions (85.39 ± 57.99 vs. 5.19 ± 2.56, P < 0.001) due to minimal physiological brain background (SUVbgd 0.09 ± 0.11). Dual-tracer imaging supplemented the detection of 15 viable tumor lesions in 9 patients that were missed by either single tracer alone, increasing per-lesion sensitivity to 100% and preventing potential underdiagnosis in 47.4% (9/19) of patients with viable disease. CONCLUSIONS: [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 PET/CT outperforms [¹⁸F]FDG in identifying viable brain metastases from lung cancer, primarily due to its exceptional tumor-to-background contrast. The complementary detection patterns of the two tracers suggest that combined use can minimize diagnostic omissions, supporting an integrative imaging paradigm for more accurate intracranial staging/restaging.
