articles.title: Anatomy-Based Simulations of B0 Field Maps: A Large Database for Head and Spine Shim Coil Development.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Static magnetic field (B0) inhomogeneity degrades MRI quality near air-tissue interfaces in the brain and spine. Anatomically tailored shim coils can mitigate these effects, but their design requires knowledge of B0 distributions across diverse human anatomies and realistic posture differences. This study aimed to create an open-source database of simulated B0 field maps derived from segmented MRI to support brain and spine shimming development. METHODS: Sixty volunteers were scanned at two 3T sites using T1-weighted MPRAGE protocols with head-to-torso coverage. Anatomical structures were segmented using three automated tools (Samseg, TotalSpineSeg, and a custom nnU-Net v2 model) to label the body, brain, skull, spine, vertebrae, discs, sinuses, trachea, and lungs. Segmentations were post-processed using a custom 3D Slicer pipeline for island removal, hole filling, and smoothing, then merged and assigned literature-based susceptibility values. ΔB0 maps were simulated via Fourier-domain convolution with the dipole kernel. Simulations were compared against measured field maps in two additional subjects. To illustrate an application, volume-wise and slice-wise shimming were performed on this simulated dataset. RESULTS: Expected inhomogeneity patterns were observed in simulated ΔB0 maps near airways. The subject-averaged spatial standard deviation of ΔB0 within the brain was reduced by 66.7% with whole-volume second-order shimming and by 70.9% with subsequent first-order slice-wise shimming. CONCLUSION: An open-source database of 60 anatomy-based simulated ΔB0 maps spanning the brain and spinal cord for shimming optimization is presented, with all data and code publicly available.

articles.title: High-Resolution Multi-Delay Renal Arterial Spin Labeling Using Radial Imaging at 5T MRI.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a high-resolution multi-delay renal arterial spin labeling (ASL) technique for free-breathing imaging at 5T. METHODS: A radial renal ASL (Radial-ASL) sequence was proposed using flow-sensitive alternating inversion recovery (FAIR) preparation followed by continuous golden-angle radial acquisition. The k-space data were firstly sorted by delay time and then reordered based on respiratory motion, with data grouped into four respiratory phases for Spatio-Temporal eXtra-Dimensional Golden-angle RAdial Sparse Parallel (ST-XD-GRASP) reconstruction. Both the Buxton kinetic model and a stepwise kinetic model were applied to perfusion quantification. The proposed method was evaluated against the saturated multi-delay ASL (SAMURAI) technique using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and correlation analysis. Scan-rescan repeatability and interobserver reproducibility were assessed using ICC. RESULTS: Twelve healthy volunteers (mean age: 27.4 ± 4.9 years old, 7 males) and one patient (55-year-old female) were included. Radial-ASL with ST-XD-GRASP provided high-quality images with 1.17 mm in-plane resolution. The stepwise model showed improved fitting performance (R2 ≥ 0.95) compared with the Buxton model (R2: 0.36-0.85). Cortical renal blood flow showed no significant difference between Radial-ASL and SAMURAI (363.7 ± 30.3 vs. 360.4 ± 30.0 mL/100 g/min, p = 0.216), with good agreement (ICC = 0.910) and strong correlation (r = 0.912). Radial-ASL demonstrated good scan-rescan repeatability (ICC = 0.884-0.911) and interobserver reproducibility (ICC = 0.943-0.985). CONCLUSION: Radial-ASL at 5T enables free-breathing multi-delay renal perfusion quantification with high spatial resolution and demonstrates good agreement with SAMURAI technique as well as good repeatability.

articles.title: Importance of Background Suppression and Post Label Delay Optimization for White Matter Perfusion Imaging Using Arterial Spin Labeling at 7 Tesla.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Ultra-high field MRI (7 Tesla) could potentially improve white matter (WM) perfusion imaging because of less severe loss of label thanks to longer T1-values. However, physiological noise increases, making background suppression (BGS) likely more important at this field strength. The aim of this study is first to assess the importance of background suppression at 7 Tesla compared to 3 Tesla, and secondly to use that knowledge to optimize flow-alternating-inversion-recovery (FAIR) ASL for WM perfusion imaging. METHODS: A background suppressed FAIR ASL labeling scheme was implemented at both 7 and 3 Tesla scanners. Perfusion temporal SNR was compared over a wide range of BGS-levels by exploiting a 2D multi-slice readout. The knowledge gained from this was used to optimize a FAIR ASL scan with 3D readout scanned at several post label delays (PLD). The tSNR was compared across PLD for GM and several WM masks. RESULTS: BGS was found to be more important at 7 Tesla compared to 3 Tesla. Therefore, a 3D FAIR ASL scan with homogeneous high BGS was used for WM perfusion imaging. Across PLD, we found a parabolic trend for significant voxels in the deep WM, both for a non-zero but slightly stronger for the ischemic perfusion threshold, peaking around a PLD of 2300 ms. However, this was not significantly higher than a PLD of 1800 and 2800 ms in this healthy population. CONCLUSION: BGS becomes increasingly important for perfusion imaging at higher field strengths. Background suppressed WM perfusion imaging at 7 Tesla might benefit from a longer PLD than typically recommended for GM.

articles.title: Pulsed Off-Resonance Saturation for Macromolecular Proton Fraction-Weighted Contrast With Intrinsic Flow Attenuation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a pulsed off-resonance magnetization transfer (MT) preparation module that achieves intrinsic flow attenuation while enabling efficient macromolecular proton fraction (MPF)-weighted contrast that specific to macromolecular pool. METHODS: In the proposed MPF-SPS (MPF-weighted contrast mapping using short pulsed saturation) approach, repetitive short off-resonance RF pulses are applied in conjunction with spoiler gradients, enabling simultaneous MT contrast generation in stationary tissue and intrinsic blood signal attenuation. An MPF-weighted relaxation rate,  R mpfsps   , is derived that is specific to the macromolecular pool and independent of the free water pool. An off-resonance Extended Phase Graph (EPG) framework incorporating MT effects was developed for efficient parameter optimization. The proposed approach is validated with EPG-based two-pool simulations, phantom, and in vivo brain studies at 3.0 T. RESULTS: Simulations showed that the off-resonance EPG-MT framework closely agrees with two-pool Bloch-McConnell simulations while requiring substantially less computation time. This efficient framework was used to optimize the sequence parameters, confirming that intrinsic flow attenuation effectively reduces partial-volume effects caused by intravascular signal contamination. Both simulations and phantom experiments demonstrated that MPF-SPS provides  R mpfsps   maps that are insensitive to free-water-pool parameters. In vivo brain imaging further demonstrated that the proposed method generates  R mpfsps   maps with MPF-weighted contrast and intrinsic flow attenuation. CONCLUSION: A novel MPF-weighted contrast imaging method using pulsed off-resonance MT preparation with intrinsic flow attenuation is proposed, providing a technical basis for future MPF-sensitive vessel wall imaging.

articles.title: A Dataset-Conditioned Visual State-Space Model with Clinical Taxonomy and Mask Guidance for Multi-Dataset Cystoscopic Image Classification.
articles.abstract: Classification of bladder lesions in cystoscopic images is difficult because datasets differ in acquisition conditions and label spaces, classes are imbalanced, and non-lesion regions can dominate the image. We propose Dataset-Conditioned Clinical-Taxonomy-Gated VMamba (DCTG-VMamba), a visual state-space model that jointly learns CystoDS, the Endoscopic Bladder Tissue Classification dataset (EBTC), and Kaggle white-light imaging (WLI) using supervision from a shared research taxonomy without clinical expert validation and dataset-conditioned fusion of mask-derived region-of-interest (ROI) and surrounding-context tokens with a global image token. After cleaning, 8067, 1611, and 1229 images were analyzed, respectively, using five-fold cross-validation with disjoint patient, file-derived case, or image groups. Three joint-training multiclass and three separately trained binary tasks were evaluated. Models included eight reference backbones, DCTG-VMamba, five prespecified ablations, and dataset-specific VMamba-T controls. The evaluation comprised 535 training runs covering primary classification, ablations, supervision-matched binary controls, and source-held-out transfer. In the initial experiments, DCTG-VMamba achieved macro-F1 scores of 0.609 ± 0.075, 0.590 ± 0.136, and 0.958 ± 0.005 on five-class CystoDS, four-class EBTC, and six-class Kaggle WLI. Repeated experiments did not establish a consistent advantage over joint VMamba-T, and the initial EBTC mean ranking was not reproduced. Binary-label-only DCTG-VMamba had higher observed macro-F1 than joint VMamba-T in all three binary tasks, but no paired difference was significant after Holm correction. Auxiliary mask supervision showed a consistent descriptive direction on CystoDS, and validation-fitted temperature scaling reduced EBTC calibration error. Transfer comparisons showed no consistent advantage over joint VMamba-T. The contribution is a unified learning framework and its controlled evaluation across heterogeneous cystoscopic label spaces.

articles.title: Multimodal Integration of Imaging and Pathological Features for Postoperative Outcome Prediction in Liver Cancer.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to construct and externally validate a multimodal radiopathomic fusion model for predicting postoperative recurrence in patients with primary liver cancer (restricted to hepatocellular carcinoma, excluding intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and mixed-type hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma) after curative hepatectomy, and to explore its independent prognostic efficacy and clinical utility. A total of 280 primary liver cancer patients from two centers were retrospectively allocated to a training cohort (n = 182) and an independent validation cohort (n = 98). Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative abdominal MRI, while pathomic features were quantified from H&E-stained whole-slide images. Eight machine learning algorithms were screened via fivefold cross‑validation for unimodal model development. The optimal random forest classifier was applied to construct unimodal radiomic‑only and pathomic‑only models, whereas the final multimodal fusion model was built using logistic regression with concatenated pre‑screened radiomic and pathomic features. ROC, SHAP, Kaplan-Meier survival, and logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess model performance, risk stratification, and independent predictors. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two cohorts. We extracted 3390 MRI radiomic and 1039 pathomic features and then built single-modal and fusion models. The fusion model outperformed unimodal models (AUC = 0.894 training, 0.858 validation). It stratified patients into low-/high-recurrence risk subgroups (HR = 9.93 and 5.32). Multivariable analysis confirmed Fusion_Risk score (HR = 18.73) as the strongest independent recurrence predictor, superior to routine clinicopathological biomarkers. The radiopathomic fusion model showed good calibration and satisfactory net clinical benefit. Compared with unimodal models, it exhibited a trend toward improved predictive performance, suggesting potential value as an independent prognostic tool for individualized postoperative recurrence surveillance in patients with primary liver cancer after curative resection.

articles.title: DiCoNet: Diagnosis-Conditioned Report Generation for Retinal OCT via Pseudo Semantic Embedding.
articles.abstract: Retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) report generation faces two major challenges: the scarcity of paired image-report data and the inherent semantic gap between visual representations and clinical concepts. Under such low-resource conditions, conventional vision-driven encoder-decoder models are prone to representation degradation and pathological hallucination, which cause semantic drift and make generated reports deviate from true clinical diagnoses. Inspired by the diagnostic workflow in clinical practice, where diagnosis precedes description, we propose a diagnosis-conditioned network, DiCoNet, which reformulates medical report generation from direct image-text mapping into a diagnosis-conditioned sequence generation task. DiCoNet adopts a two-stage progressive training strategy. It first learns robust and discriminative visual representations from a large-scale diagnostic classification dataset and then performs partial fine-tuning on limited report data. To bridge the gap between visual representations and diagnostic semantics, we design a pseudo semantic embedding (PSE) module that injects continuous diagnostic priors directly into the visual prefix, guiding report generation without increasing the prefix length. We further introduce an auxiliary diagnostic supervision branch to maintain feature discriminability during decoding and enable end-to-end autonomous inference without external labels at test time. Extensive experiments on a real-world clinical OCT dataset show that DiCoNet achieves the best scores among the evaluated methods on most automatic evaluation metrics, with a ROUGE-L score of 0.420 and a CIDEr score of 0.951. Expert evaluation and an OCT-specific clinical error analysis further support the accuracy and completeness of DiCoNet-generated reports, highlighting its potential for assisting OCT report drafting.

articles.title: A Deep Learning Framework Integrating Multi-Region Radiomics and Clinical Features for Improved Breast Ultrasound Lesion Classification.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer poses a substantial global burden on women's health, making accurate early differentiation of benign and malignant breast lesions essential for improving prognosis and reducing healthcare costs. Although deep learning methods have been widely developed for breast ultrasound lesion classification, most rely on imaging information alone. Existing approaches incorporating peritumoral information often use empirically defined regions, while clinical characteristics are rarely integrated into end-to-end frameworks, limiting the use of complementary diagnostic information. To address these limitations, we propose Multi-Source Information Fusion DenseNet (MSIF-DenseNet), an end-to-end framework for breast ultrasound lesion classification. It jointly integrates intratumoral ultrasound images, peritumoral regions, and structured clinical information. Specifically, a dual-stream convolutional architecture with separable convolutions independently learns representative features from the intratumoral and peritumoral regions, while a multi-layer perceptron branch encodes patient clinical characteristics. The resulting imaging and clinical features are subsequently fused through a Compact Bilinear Pooling (CBP) module to capture high-order interactions among heterogeneous information sources for benign-malignant classification. On a private dataset comprising 500 breast ultrasound images from 500 patients, MSIF-DenseNet achieved an AUC of 84.21 % ± 3.52 %  , F1-score of 83.81 % ± 3.40 %  , and accuracy of 80.00 % ± 3.90 %  under five-fold cross-validation. Compared with the imaging-only dual-stream baseline, integrating clinical information increased AUC and F1-score by 4.13 and 2.69 percentage points (pp), respectively, while integration of multi-region information increased AUC and F1-score by 9.86 and 6.09 pp, respectively, over the best single-region model. These results support the effectiveness of combining multi-region ultrasound information with clinical data for breast ultrasound lesion classification.

articles.title: Reducing Demographic Bias in Medical Imaging Using Siamese Representation Learning.
articles.abstract: Deep learning models for medical imaging often exhibit demographic bias, leading to performance disparities across protected groups such as age, gender, and race. This study proposes a debiasing framework to reduce such disparities while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. We propose a Siamese neural network trained using triplet loss, where demographic attributes are incorporated into triplet selection to encourage separation by disease class while promoting within-class similarity across demographic groups. The method was evaluated on pleural effusion detection using chest X-rays (109,005 images from 41,063 patients) and Alzheimer's disease classification using brain MRI (1494 scans from 348 patients). Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), precision, and true positive rate, along with equalized odds difference. The proposed method significantly reduced demographic disparities while maintaining or improving overall predictive performance compared with baseline and existing debiasing approaches. In pleural effusion detection, true positive rate gaps were reduced by 32% (race), 8% (age), and 22% (gender). In Alzheimer's disease classification, the true positive rate gap was reduced by 41% (age). Model interpretation indicated clinically meaningful imaging features were used for decision-making. Demographic-aware triplet sampling within a Siamese framework can effectively mitigate demographic performance disparities in medical imaging models while maintaining competitive overall diagnostic performance, suggesting potential for more equitable and clinically reliable deployment of medical imaging AI systems.

articles.title: Knowledge-Guided Fine-Grained Self-Supervised Multimodal Representation Learning for MRI-Visible Endolymphatic Hydrops Assessment in Ménière's Disease.
articles.abstract: Ménière's disease (MD) is a clinically defined inner-ear disorder with heterogeneous manifestations, for which MRI-visible endolymphatic hydrops (EH) is an imaging finding rather than a sufficient diagnostic criterion. We developed a multimodal pretraining framework that combines anatomically constrained representation learning from inner-ear MRI with ontology-normalized concepts extracted from radiology reports. Evaluation used five patient-disjoint outer folds comprising 524 patients (1048 ears) and focused on ear-level MRI-visible EH assessment rather than MD diagnosis. With 10% of the downstream labels, SMAM-MD achieved an AUC of 87.95 ± 1.84 %  , 3.30 percentage points above the strongest displayed baseline mean; under full supervision, its AUC was 98.40 ± 0.72 %  , compared with 98.65 ± 0.65 %  for DINOv2 FT. For prediction of six discharge hearing thresholds from inner-ear MRI and admission audiometry, SMAM-MD achieved an overall macro-MAE of 6.83 ± 0.33   dB HL, compared with 7.47 ± 0.36   dB HL for DINOv2 FT (Holm-adjusted P = 0.000570  ). These findings support improved label efficiency and lower discharge-threshold prediction error within this single-center cohort; they do not establish MRI-based MD diagnosis, causal treatment effects, or external clinical generalizability.

articles.title: Retinex Algorithm-Based Automated Quantification of Eight Key Reflux Signs and Overall Score of Laryngopharyngeal Reflux Disease.
articles.abstract: The Reflux Finding Score (RFS) is a widely used laryngoscopy-based instrument for assessing laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD); however, its reliance on subjective interpretation leads to considerable inter-observer variability. In this study, we propose TM-Net, a computer-vision framework for automated LPRD assessment. To address three key clinical challenges in automated RFS scoring-uneven illumination, robust feature representation, and anatomically grounded fine-grained scoring-TM-Net integrates three key components. First, MSRCR-based image enhancement normalizes illumination variations and enhances subtle pathological signs. Second, a ResNet-50 encoder with a local self-attention (LSA) module extracts robust features and captures both local and global representations. Third, a segmentation network (TS-Net) delineates seven laryngeal anatomical regions to provide explicit spatial priors, and a feature fusion strategy (CLIA) combined with a multi-label classification network (MLC-Net) simultaneously predicts item-specific ordinal scores for all eight RFS sub-items according to the RFS criteria, enabling fine-grained quantification instead of coarse binary classification. These designs improve performance by addressing illumination variations, enhancing feature representation, and imposing anatomical constraints for comprehensive sub-item scoring. TS-Net achieved a mean intersection over union of 0.7975 and an F1 score of 0.8581 across seven laryngeal regions. Using 24-h multichannel intraluminal impedance-pH monitoring as the reference standard, TM-Net achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 90.91%, with substantial agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.75) and no significant discordance (McNemar's test, P = 1.000). These results indicate that TM-Net provides an objective and standardized tool for LPRD screening.

articles.title: A Dual-View Context-Aware Framework for Automated Bone Lesion Segmentation and Quantification in Whole-Body Planar Bone Scintigraphy.
articles.abstract: Whole-body planar bone scintigraphy reflects skeletal metabolic activity throughout the body and is widely used for the assessment of bone metastases. However, automatic segmentation of hypermetabolic bone lesions remains challenging because of low image contrast, limited spatial resolution, and complex lesion distributions. In this study, we proposed a dual-view context-aware framework that employed Bone-Segnet, a segmentation network integrating multiscale feature modeling, global context modeling, and view-conditioned modulation to improve lesion representation and segmentation. The study included whole-body planar bone scintigraphy images from 932 patients, with hypermetabolic bone lesions manually delineated on anterior and posterior images by experienced nuclear medicine physicians. The proposed network effectively segmented hypermetabolic bone lesions with complex distributions. In performance comparisons, it achieved the best segmentation performance among the evaluated baseline models, with the dice score showing the largest improvement from 0.7440 to 0.8750. In a preliminary reader efficiency evaluation involving two experienced nuclear medicine physicians, the average annotation time decreased from 38.20 s/image to 18.41 s/image under a model-assisted workflow involving automatic segmentation followed by manual correction, representing a 51.81% reduction. Quantitative analysis of the segmentation results yielded image-derived descriptors, including connected-component counts and total segmented pixel counts, across disease types. These results suggest that the proposed framework achieves improved segmentation performance for hypermetabolic bone lesions relative to the evaluated baseline models and may reduce annotation workload, thereby providing a basis for downstream quantitative imaging analysis in whole-body planar bone scintigraphy.

articles.title: Eye-Tracking-Guided Tri-View Learning for Fine-Grained Medical Image Classification and Segmentation.
articles.abstract: Fine-grained medical image analysis involves two core tasks: image-level disease classification and pixel-level border delineation, both requiring intelligent models to capture subtle lesion-relevant visual cues. We investigate a shared gaze-guided multi-view design principle through separate task-specific classification and segmentation models. For classification, gaze heatmaps are used to derive point prompts and construct global, lesion-core, and peri-lesional views, enabling the model to integrate whole-image context, lesion-dominant details, and surrounding tissue information. In addition, a dual-path diagnosis module is designed to combine direct prediction of disease classes with hierarchical lesion-dominant subtype refinement. For segmentation, we introduce Tri-view Gaze-prior Input (TVGP-Input), a plug-and-play input-level module that introduces eye-tracking-derived spatial priors to segmentation backbones without modifying their encoder-decoder structures. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 0.8680 ± 0.0236  , a macro-F1 score of 0.7255 ± 0.0425  , a weighted F1 score of 0.8531 ± 0.0195  , and macro- and micro-averaged areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.8968 ± 0.0358  and 0.9668 ± 0.0199  in five-fold cross-validation on three-class medical image classification. In segmentation experiments, the proposed TVGP-Input enhanced tri-view segmentation model achieves a Dice score of 0.9285 ± 0.0109  and an intersection over union of 0.8694 ± 0.0144  . These results support gaze-guided learning within the evaluated breast ultrasound classification and prostate magnetic resonance imaging segmentation settings.

articles.title: AI-Assisted Multimodal Imaging Integration for Individualized Transseptal Puncture Planning During Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
articles.abstract: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is a critical step during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, and accurate anatomical understanding of the interatrial septum is essential for individualized procedural planning. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) provides real-time visualization of septal anatomy but is limited by its two-dimensional representation and operator dependence. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multimodal imaging framework integrating preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) with intraoperative ICE to provide patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) anatomical guidance for TSP planning. This single-center study enrolled 700 patients undergoing AF ablation. An AI framework was developed using data from 500 patients to perform automated segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and CTA-ICE multimodal image integration. The framework was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort of 200 patients. The primary outcome was the influence of AI-assisted anatomical information on individualized TSP planning, assessed by changes in puncture strategy following AI-assisted assessment. Secondary outcomes included decision confidence, planning time, interreader agreement, and procedural feasibility. The AI framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient of 0.854 for automated anatomical segmentation and a Dice coefficient of 0.862 for 3D left atrial reconstruction. In the temporal validation cohort, at least one AI-recommended adjustment was incorporated into the final TSP strategy in 68 patients (34.0%). The recommendations addressed involved three key components of TSP planning: puncture site category in 52 patients (26.0%), puncture direction in 61 patients (30.5%), and puncture trajectory or angle in 74 patients (37.0%). AI-assisted assessment increased decision confidence (4.3 ± 0.6 vs. 3.4 ± 0.8, p < 0.001), reduced planning time (28.7 ± 10.3 vs. 42.5 ± 15.2 s, p < 0.001), and improved interreader agreement for anatomical assessment. In the temporal validation cohort, acute successful TSP was achieved in 196 patients (98.0%), with a mean transseptal time of 6.8-2.5 min and an overall complication rate of 3.0%. AI-assisted integration of preprocedural CTA with intraoperative ICE provides patient-specific 3D anatomical information that supports individualized TSP planning. The proposed framework demonstrated feasibility and compatibility with anatomical assessment and procedural planning, hopefully contributing to improve procedural or clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Spectral Decorrelation of Glutamate for Clinical Proton Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Although glutamate (Glu) plays a central role in many neuropsychiatric disorders, MRS measurement of Glu often suffers from confounding correlations due to spectral overlap, adversely affecting subsequent clinical correlational analysis. This study aimed to optimize the commonly used 3 T PRESS method to minimize the overall Glu spectral correlation with other neurometabolites. METHODS: Monte Carlo simulations combined with a mathematical model of spectral fitting were used to evaluate spectral correlations between Glu and other metabolites. The optimal {TE1, TE} pair minimizing the overall Glu correlation was identified and validated by analyzing in vivo measurement of Glu in the anterior cingulate cortex. The robustness of the optimization was further assessed under varying spectral linewidths and altered metabolite concentrations. RESULTS: The optimal {TE1, TE} values for 4, 6, 8, and 10 Hz linewidth were found to be {42, 100}, {40, 95}, {38, 94}, and {38, 90} ms, respectively. These optimal {TE1, TE} pairs reduced the overall Glu spectral correlation coefficient to less than 0.05, corresponding to a negligible effect size. This reduction was consistently observed in both Monte Carlo simulations and analysis of in vivo measurements and remained robust across metabolite level variations typically seen in bipolar disorder, methamphetamine use disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and hepatic encephalopathy. CONCLUSION: Systematic optimization of the {TE1, TE} pair enables decorrelation of Glu MRS measurement at 3 Tesla by effectively minimizing confounding spectral correlations among brain metabolites. The proposed approach provides a robust and clinically applicable framework that decorrelates Glu MRS measurements for viable downstream clinical analyses.

articles.title: Quantifying inter-surgeon variation in computed tomography-based preoperative planning for total hip arthroplasty.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Three-dimensional (3D) preoperative planning is essential in total hip arthroplasty (THA) to optimize implant alignment and reduce the risk of impingement-related complications such as dislocation. Although recent technological advances, including computed tomography (CT)-based navigation and robotic-assisted surgery, have improved the accuracy of implant placement, variation in preoperative planning among surgeons remains poorly understood. This study aimed to quantify inter-surgeon variation in 3D preoperative THA planning and to evaluate the impact of stem design on this variation. METHODS: Eleven hip surgeons independently performed 3D preoperative planning for 50 THA cases using a CT-based planning system. The cases included two stem types: tapered wedge stems and anatomical stems. Implant size was fixed, and planning was performed according to the combined anteversion theory. Inter-surgeon variation in implant orientation and position was quantified using the mean pairwise absolute difference (MPD) and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). The surgeon-selected cup-stem anteversion combinations were grouped into five categories, and inter-surgeon agreement was assessed using Fleiss' kappa coefficient. RESULTS: Angular MPDs ranged from 0.8° to 3.8°, with the greatest variation observed in stem anteversion. Positional MPDs ranged from 0.8 to 2.1 mm, with the largest variation observed along the stem craniocaudal axis. The ICCs ranged from 0.69 to 0.99. Agreement in cup-stem anteversion categories was moderate (kappa = 0.44). When the two stem groups were compared, no significant differences in angular variation were observed, while only limited differences in positional variation were found. CONCLUSION: Inter-surgeon variation assessed by MPD provided a direct measure of the absolute magnitude of differences among surgeons' plans. Our findings demonstrate that noticeable inter-surgeon variation exists in preoperative THA planning despite high agreement coefficients. Quantitative benchmarks derived from these data may be useful for evaluating planning consistency and for validating emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence-based automated THA planning systems.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Top 5 Publications by Radiology Faculty by 5-Year Intervals in All Specialties Since 2000.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To identify the 5 most well-cited manuscripts written by American radiologists across 5 time periods from 2000 to 2025 within 10 disciplines of radiology and to characterize those manuscripts, authors, journals in which they were published, and institutions of origin. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional bibliometric study, American academic radiology faculty rosters were compiled from 174 institutions, yielding 7366 members. Their 248,754 Scopus-indexed manuscripts were screened, and the most-cited publications in each of 5 windows (2000-2005, 2006-2010, 2011-2015, 2016-2020, 2021-2025) were screened for those publications where radiology faculty occupied first or last author positions. The radiology subspecialty was assigned by manuscript content by subspecialty journal, weighted MeSH (Medical Subject Headings) scoring, and large language model classification-with manual verification of top-ranked articles. The 5 most-cited manuscripts were selected in 10 radiology subspecialties, per timeframe, yielding 250 papers. RESULTS: The 250 manuscripts were anchored by 205 radiologists; 49 authors contributed more than one paper, and 4 authors contributed 5 or more top manuscripts. Compared with the full roster, anchor authors were more often full professors (78.1% vs 24.5%), MD-PhDs (17.1% vs 5.8%), and men (73.2% vs 65.9%, P = 0.04). Neuroradiology accounted for the highest cumulative median citation count (1568), double that of the next field, cardiothoracic imaging (739). Radiology published 57 manuscripts, but general medical journals such as NEJM and JAMA yielded higher median citations. Four institutions contributed >10 of the first-authored papers. CONCLUSION: Radiologists' most-cited literature is dominated by senior authors who often publish multiple high-ranking papers, favoring select institutions, topics, and journals.

articles.title: Three-Dimensional T2-Weighted Variable Flip-Angle Turbo Spin Echo for Cervical Spine MRI at 0.55 T: A Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of three-dimensional T2-weighted sampling perfection with application-optimized contrasts using different flip angle evolutions (SPACE) for cervical spine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at 0.55 T and to preliminarily compare image quality with conventional two-dimensional T2-weighted turbo spin echo (TSE) in healthy volunteers and post-anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) subjects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Five healthy volunteers (26.6 ± 2.9 years) and five post-ACDF subjects with titanium implants (63.6 ± 7.2 years) underwent cervical spine MRI at 0.55 T using sagittal TSE, axial TSE, and sagittal SPACE. Quantitative analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) efficiency and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-to-spinal cord (SC) contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) efficiency. Two board-certified radiologists independently evaluated perceived SNR, CSF pulsation artifacts, motion artifacts, visualization of ten anatomical structures, and metal artifact severity using a 5-point Likert scale. Quantitative sequence comparisons were performed using exact paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests at the subject level. Qualitative 5-point scores were analyzed separately by cohort and category using linear mixed-effects models that accounted for subject and reader clustering. RESULTS: 3D SPACE demonstrated higher SNR efficiency than 2D TSE for both CSF and SC in both cohorts. CSF-SC CNR efficiency was higher with SPACE. In healthy subjects, 3D SPACE received higher reader scores for intraspinal nerve root visualization and CSF pulsation artifact reduction. In post-ACDF subjects, 3D SPACE received higher reader scores for nerve root visualization, whereas metal-artifact scores and other qualitative metrics did not show clear sequence-related differences. CONCLUSION: 3D SPACE at 0.55 T is feasible for cervical spine MRI in healthy subjects and post-ACDF subjects with titanium instrumentation. Although diagnostic performance was not evaluated, the preliminary findings suggest potential advantages of SPACE, including higher SNR/CNR efficiency, improved CSF signal homogeneity with reduced CSF pulsation artifacts, and improved nerve root visualization, supporting further evaluation.

articles.title: STAT Priority Labeling in a Large-Scale CT Cohort: Frequency, Predictors, and Turnaround Time Associations.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Indiscriminate STAT labeling can erode the priority system's ability to distinguish clinically urgent from nonurgent computed tomography (CT) examinations, straining radiologist worklists and delaying interpretation of genuinely urgent studies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study assessed 500,000 STAT CT examinations performed in 2025 at RadPartners (Radiology Partners, El Segundo, California, USA) imaging centers. After exclusion of duplicate records and examinations with insufficient clinical documentation, 365,676 examinations across four cohorts (head, chest, abdomen/pelvis, and combined chest-abdomen-pelvis [CAP] CT) underwent indication-based STAT appropriateness classification. Associations with place of service, reporting shift, and day type were evaluated using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression. Report turnaround times were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. Temporal trends from 2019 to 2026 were assessed using linear regression. RESULTS: Of 365,676 examinations, 85,958 (23.51%) were classified as potentially inappropriate STAT. Rates were highest for CAP CT (31.01%) and chest CT (29.61%), followed by head CT (26.84%) and abdomen/pelvis CT (15.45%). Outpatient setting was the strongest independent predictor, particularly for CAP CT (odds ratio [OR], 72.09; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 64.77, 80.23) and chest CT (OR, 30.57; 95% CI: 29.01, 32.21). Potentially inappropriate STAT cases had longer turnaround times than appropriate STAT cases across all cohorts, most pronounced for chest CT (median, 975 minutes vs 37 minutes). A significant upward temporal trend was identified (+0.47% points per year; R² = 0.57; P = 0.036). CONCLUSION: Nearly one in four STAT CT examinations lacked a documented urgent indication, with overuse concentrated in outpatient settings and daytime workflows, supporting targeted STAT stewardship interventions.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Arterial Spin-Labeling MRI in the Presurgical Evaluation of Focal Epilepsy and the Limits of Current Evidence for Predicting Surgical Outcome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Arterial spin-labeling (ASL) MR imaging is a noninvasive perfusion technique used in presurgical evaluation of focal epilepsy. A 2021 meta-analysis assessed its accuracy for identifying perfusion abnormalities concordant with the epileptogenic zone (EZ) but predated later studies and partly derived specificity from healthy-control true negatives. We re-estimated the diagnostic accuracy of ASL for EZ-concordant perfusion abnormalities with explicit handling of true negatives, and tested whether current data permit a quantitative estimate of the relationship between ASL findings and postsurgical seizure freedom. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-DTA, we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Scopus from inception to June 2026 for English-language primary studies (≥10 patients) of ASL for EZ localization or surgical-outcome evaluation in focal epilepsy. Random-effects models estimated pooled sensitivity (logit; primary), an exploratory specificity, a logit concordance/detection proportion, and a Freeman-Tukey seizure-free proportion. Because true negatives were absent by design, a joint bivariate/HSROC model was not estimable. Risk of bias used QUADAS-2 and QUIPS; certainty of evidence used a DTA-adapted GRADE approach. RESULTS: Fifteen studies were included. The primary analysis (8 studies, 160 patients) yielded a pooled ASL sensitivity for EZ-concordant abnormalities of 0.73 (95% CI, 0.65-0.80; I2 = 0.0%). The concordance/detection proportion was 0.78 (95% CI, 0.62-0.89; 4 studies), and exploratory specificity 0.37 (95% CI, 0.13-0.71; 5 studies). In the surgical-outcome arm, the pooled seizure-free proportion (Engel I/ILAE 1) was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.58-0.77; 4 studies) and 0.71 (95% CI, 0.56-0.84) in a stricter analysis. Critically, a pooled odds ratio for seizure freedom in ASL-concordant versus ASL-discordant resections could not be computed: the required cross-tabulation was reported in no study. CONCLUSIONS: ASL has moderate, stable sensitivity for identifying perfusion abnormalities concordant with the anatomo-electro-clinically defined EZ, whereas specificity is not estimable from current single-group designs. ASL-linked surgical cohorts achieve seizure freedom in two-thirds of operated patients, but whether ASL-resection concordance predicts seizure freedom is unquantifiable: a reporting gap, not a null result. Until outcome is reported stratified by ASL-resection concordance, ASL should be used as a localizing adjunct, not a prognostic marker.

articles.title: Reversal of Late Gadolinium Enhancement MRI-Assessed Left Atrial Fibrosis Following Cardioversion in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) cardioversion may reverse atrial remodeling. PURPOSE: To investigate whether LGE-MRI-assessed left atrial (LA) fibrosis regresses after persistent atrial fibrillation (PersAF) cardioversion to sinus rhythm, and to analyze the relationship between fibrosis change and traditional volume-based measures of LA reverse remodeling. STUDY TYPE: Prospective. POPULATION: Fifty-three patients following cardioversion for PersAF. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T, cine balanced steady-state free precession cine and 3D inversion recovery gradient-echo sequences. ASSESSMENT: MRI was performed 1-3 days after AF-cardioversion (early follow-up), and again at 3 months (late follow-up). Image analysis was performed by two observers using CVI42 and ADAS software. Data were compared between early and late follow-up. LA fibrosis on LGE-MRI was categorized by the image intensity ratio (IIR): core zone (IIR > 1.61) and border zone (0.97 < IIR ≤ 1.61). Maximum LA volume (LAVmax), LA ejection fraction (LAEF), LA strain, and left ventricular mass were assessed from cine data. An LAVmax reduction ≥ 15% from early to late follow-up defined LA reverse remodeling. STATISTICAL TESTS: Early and late follow-up data were compared using paired t-tests. Multivariable analysis was performed to assess the associations between changes in LA border and core zone and other LA parameters. A p-value < 0.05 was considered significant. RESULTS: Seventeen patients had volume-based LA reverse. Compared with early follow-up, LA border zone (22.2 [11.8-37.0] vs. 18.1 [11.8-25.2] cm2) and core zone (0.9 ± 3.0 vs. 0.1 ± 0.6 cm2) were significantly decreased. LAVmax was significantly reduced (97.2 ± 26.3 vs. 109.4 ± 32.7 mL), and LAEF (44.1 ± 15.8 vs. 32.2% ± 13.1%) and LA strain (27.4 ± 14.1 vs. 18.2% ± 8.6%) improved. Volume-based LA reverse remodeling was unrelated to ΔLA border (p = 0.955) or Δcore zone (p = 0.301). DATA CONCLUSION: PersAF conversion to sinus rhythm resulted in a reduction in LGE-defined atrial enhancement, LAV reduction, and improved function. Fibrosis regression was independent of volume-based LA reverse remodeling. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 4.

articles.title: Single arm, Multicenter Phase II Study Investigating the Efficacy and Safety of a Novel Therapeutic Scheme in Patients with Unresectable Cholangiocarcinoma; Radioembolization in Combination with CisGem and Durvalumab (MEDI4736) PM-CARE.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive malignancy associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT), also known as transarterial radioembolization (TARE), may improve locoregional tumor control and enhance antitumor immune response, increasing the efficacy of systemic treatment. This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of upfront TARE followed by cisplatin, gemcitabine and durvalumab in treatment-naïve patients with unresectable liver-predominant iCCA. PROTOCOL: PM-CARE is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm phase II study. Treatment-naïve eligible patients with upfront unresectable liver-predominant iCCA preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A), Eastern Cooperative Oncology performance status 0-1. Following angiographic mapping and technetium-99 m macroaggregated albumin (99mTc-MAA) simulation, participants undergo personalized dosimetry-guided SIRT. Systemic treatment with cisplatin, gemcitabine and durvalumab will start 21 days after TARE and administered for six cycles. Co-primary endpoints are overall response rate (ORR) at 6 months according to modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST) and safety. Secondary endpoints include ORR on target lesion and overall by RECIST 1.1, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality-of-life. Tissue and blood-based biomarkers including tumor mutational burden, circulating tumor DNA, immune profiling and cytokine characterization will be explored. STATISTICS: A sample size of 22 achieves 90.9% power to detect a difference of 0.30 in response rate using a one-sided exact test with a significance level of 0.05 at the primary endpoint. The drop-out inflated enrollment sample size is 28 participants. DISCUSSION: This study will provide prospective efficacy and safety data of upfront TARE combined with current first-line chemoimmunotherapy in patients with unresectable liver-predominant iCCA. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials.gov NCT06375915.

articles.title: Low-dose photon-counting detector CT for assessment of joint space narrowing in peripheral inflammatory arthritis: an accuracy and reliability study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess the performance of a low-dose high-resolution photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) protocol for evaluating joint space width (JSW) and joint space narrowing (JSN) in peripheral arthritis, including inter-reader reliability and comparison with digital radiography (DR) and digital tomosynthesis (DT), using standard-dose PCD-CT as the reference standard. METHODS: Twenty patients (forty hands) were examined using DR, DT, and low- and standard-dose ultra-high-resolution PCD-CT. JSW was measured, and JSN was subjectively scored in the radioulnar, radiocarpal, intercarpal, carpometacarpal, metacarpal, metacarpophalangeal, and interphalangeal joints. Two readers independently assessed all examinations, and inter-reader reliability was evaluated. DR, DT, and low-dose PCD-CT were compared with standard-dose PCD-CT. Effective doses were calculated from dose-length product and dose-area product values. Statistical analysis included linear mixed-effects models and one-way ANOVA. RESULTS: Inter-reader reliability for JSW measurements was excellent across all modalities (ICC 0.988-0.995; 95% CI 0.987-0.995). Compared with standard-dose PCD-CT, DR significantly overestimated JSW (mean difference + 0.279 mm, p < 0.001) and underestimated JSN severity. No significant differences were observed between low- and standard-dose PCD-CT for JSW (mean difference - 0.016 mm, p = 0.302) or JSN scores (mean difference + 0.019, p = 0.533). DT and standard-dose PCD-CT had higher effective doses than DR and low-dose PCD-CT, with no significant dose difference between DR and low-dose PCD-CT (p = 0.993). CONCLUSION: Low-dose PCD-CT demonstrated excellent inter-reader reliability and close agreement with standard-dose PCD-CT for JSW and JSN assessment. Compared with DR, it provided joint space measurements more consistent with standard-dose PCD-CT at a comparable effective radiation dose.

articles.title: Assessment of ulnar nerve viscoelasticity in patients with cubital tunnel syndrome using a novel ultrasound technique.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To quantify the stiffness and viscosity of the ulnar nerve using ultrasound viscoelastic imaging (UVI) and determine whether UVI is useful for diagnosing and staging cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS). METHODS: This study included 106 CuTS patients (141 elbows) and 25 healthy controls (50 elbows). CuTS severity was categorized as mild, moderate, or severe based on nerve electrodiagnostic testing results. Each participant was examined using UVI to measure the elastic modulus (E) and viscosity (Vi) of the ulnar nerve. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis and by calculating the sensitivity and specificity at the optimal cut-off values for E and Vi. The areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using DeLong's test. RESULTS: The Vi and E of the ulnar nerve at the medial epicondyle were significantly greater in the CuTS group (mean, 2.42 Pa⋅s and 40.96 kPa, respectively) than in the control group (mean, 1.34 Pa⋅s and 19.56 kPa, respectively) (p < 0.01) or even in the mild CuTS group. The Vi and E values are greater in the severe CuTS group (mean, 3.46 Pa⋅s and 55.70 kPa, respectively) than in the mild and moderate CuTS groups (mean, 1.75 Pa⋅s and 29.47 kPa; 1.96 Pa⋅s and 36.64 kPa, respectively; p < 0.01). The cut-off values for the diagnosis of CuTS at the medial epicondyle were 27.64 kPa for E and 1.69 Pa⋅s for Vi. The sensitivity and specificity of the combination of the Vi and E were 85% and 90.1%, respectively, with an AUC of 0.912 (95% CI, 0.784-0.963). CONCLUSIONS: The stiffness and viscosity of the ulnar nerve are significantly greater in CuTS patients. UVI seems to be a reliable and simple quantitative technique for diagnosing ulnar neuropathy and stratifying severe cases.

articles.title: Prognostic value of CT-derived perioperative sarcopenia and visceral fat obesity for survival in colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Sarcopenia and visceral fat obesity (VFO) are risk factors for adverse postoperative outcomes in colorectal cancer (CRC). This study investigated perioperative changes in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue in CRC patients and their predictive value for long-term survival. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cohort study enrolled stage I-III CRC patients who received upfront curative resection. Pre- and postoperative CT scans were obtained to quantify the skeletal muscle index (SMI) for sarcopenia assessment and the visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio (VSR) for VFO assessment. Landmark analyses were performed at 3 and 12 months postoperatively. Overall survival (OS) was set as the primary survival endpoint. RESULTS: A total of 266 patients (median [interquartile range, IQR] age, 55 [50-62] years; 156 males) were included. Landmark Cox regression analyses showed that sarcopenia at baseline and 3 months postoperatively was an independent risk factor for OS (hazard ratio [HR]: 3.408, p = 0.001; HR: 2.497, p = 0.016). VFO at baseline and 3 months postoperatively correlated with poorer OS in the univariable analysis (HR: 1.803, p = 0.026; HR: 1.905, p = 0.030). Integrated prediction models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.799 at baseline and 0.774 at 3 months postoperatively for OS. CONCLUSION: Sarcopenia at baseline and 3 months postoperatively is an independent risk factor for inferior OS, whereas VFO is associated with poorer OS only at the univariable level. Combining perioperative sarcopenia and VFO with clinical factors could assist in the prognostic stratification for stage I-III CRC patients following surgical resection. KEY POINTS: Question The prognostic influence of perioperative changes in CT-derived skeletal muscle and adipose tissues on colorectal cancer survival remains unclear. Findings Sarcopenia and VFO at baseline and the 3-month postoperative landmark are associated with worse overall survival and add incremental prognostic value to conventional clinical risk indicators. Critical relevance statement This work highlights the prognostic value of perioperative CT-derived sarcopenia and VFO for stage I-III CRC, suggesting that opportunistic body composition assessment on routine surveillance scans could provide valuable insights for future clinical risk stratification and management strategies.

articles.title: Parents' experiences with postmortem imaging in perinatal mortality.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Little is known about how parents experience postmortem imaging of their baby or how these investigations influence their decision-making and overall experience of care. OBJECTIVE: To explore parents' experiences with postmortem imaging following perinatal death and how these investigations influenced their decision-making and experience of care. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between June and July 2026, participants for a questionnaire were recruited through Stille Levens. The closed Facebook community, which has approximately 2,100 members and its social media channels, reaching an estimated 6,000-10000 unique followers was used. Responses to multiple-choice questions were analysed descriptively, and frequencies were calculated using Microsoft Forms. Responses to open-ended questions were analysed independently, and recurring themes produced a consensus summary. RESULTS: A total of 120 parents completed the questionnaire. The most frequently reported reason for consenting to investigations was the wish to understand why their baby had died. Among those who had experience with radiological investigations, 50% (15/30) respondents reported that these investigations had been helpful. Across the questionnaire, the quality of information and communication emerged as the dominant theme. Some parents specifically commented on the way their baby was handled during magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) examinations. Many respondents also reported insufficient follow-up care after the investigations. CONCLUSION: This study supports the importance of offering postmortem imaging as an option following perinatal death. However, our findings indicate a need for better information and communication, which should be addressed in the updated guideline. Our findings also indicate that the entire process of care following the loss of a baby should be of the highest standard, including clear information, sensitive communication, timely diagnostics, respectful handling of the baby, and appropriate aftercare.

articles.title: Late first and early second trimester fetal lung volumes assessed by MRI: normative measurements from 12 weeks to 19 weeks of gestation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Reference values and validated measurement of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based total fetal lung volume (TFLV) in the late first and early second trimester are limited. Commonly used Meyers and Rypens prediction models were developed using later gestational ages and may not apply to pregnancies imaged at 12-19 weeks. OBJECTIVE: To determine weekly reference values for TFLV between 12-week and 19-week gestation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study of fetal MRI examinations from 2009 to 2023. Of 311 examinations identified, 128 fetuses met inclusion criteria after exclusions for motion/technical limitations and conditions affecting lung development. Two radiologists manually segmented fetal lungs in two planes to obtain TFLV. Week-specific summary statistics and regression modeling were used to derive reference values and a predictive formula. Observed TFLV was compared with values predicted by the Meyers and Rypens models using t tests. Equivalence testing assessed one-plane versus two-plane average measurements, and interobserver/intraobserver agreement was evaluated using concordance correlation coefficients (CCC). RESULTS: Mean TFLV increased nonlinearly from 12 weeks to 19 weeks; the best-fit formula was TFLV (mL)=0.000001810×(gestational age in weeks)5.196. Meyers and Rypens models significantly overestimated observed means at all gestational weeks (all P<0.001). One-plane and two-plane average measurements were equivalent (TOST P<0.001), and TFLV did not differ significantly by imaging plane. Agreement was high (interobserver CCC 0.96; intraobserver CCC 0.95). CONCLUSION: Fetal MRI TFLV measurement in the late first and early second trimester is reproducible using either a one-plane approach or the average of two planes. Observed TFLV values at 12-19 weeks were significantly lower than those predicted by commonly used later-gestation models (Meyers and Rypens). These early-gestation reference values may be used cautiously in selected clinical settings, with prospective validation in independent cohorts warranted.

articles.title: Laplace-Mixture Dipole Inversion for Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop an automatic dipole inversion method for quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) that preserves fine anatomical structures without the need for manual regularization-parameter tuning. THEORY: The original approximate message passing with parameter estimation (AMP-PE) framework models image gradients with a single Laplace prior, which does not fully capture the heavy-tailed gradient distribution of brain susceptibility maps. To address this limitation, we propose a Laplace-Mixture Dipole Inversion (LAMDI) method by incorporating a two-component Laplace mixture prior into the AMP-PE framework with automatic regularization-parameter-estimation. METHODS: LAMDI was evaluated on a public in vivo dataset and the simulated calcification dataset from QSM Challenge 2.0. Its performance was compared with FANSI, MEDI, and AMP-PE with a single-Laplace prior (AMP-PE-L1) under both standard default and reference-tuned settings. Reproducible code is available at: https://github.com/shuai-huang/lamdi. RESULTS: On the public in vivo dataset, LAMDI achieved NRMSE and SSIM comparable to AMP-PE-L1 while substantially reducing HFEN. Under reference-based tuning, FANSI and MEDI achieved the best performance for some metrics, but LAMDI remained competitive without requiring reference maps or manual regularization tuning. CONCLUSION: LAMDI provides an effective and automatic regularization-parameter-estimation alternative for QSM dipole inversion by combining competitive reconstruction accuracy with improved preservation of anatomical details.

articles.title: Multi-Echo Versus T2-Prepared pCASL: Methodological Considerations for Measuring Water Transport Across the Blood-Brain Barrier.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: T2-based pCASL measures water transport across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) by separating signal from intravascular and extravascular label based on the distinct T2 relaxation times of blood and tissue. Two commonly used approaches encode T2 information differently: Multi-echo sequences employ a multi-echo turbo spin-echo readout, whereas T2-prepared (T2-prep) sequences apply a preparation module consisting of multiple 180° refocusing pulses prior to a single-echo readout. It remains unclear which approach provides more reliable estimates of BBB water exchange. This study directly compares them in terms of T2 estimation and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). METHODS: In vivo experiments implemented each method separately, as well as in a single combined sequence, using Hadamard-encoded multi-post-labeling delay (PLDs = 600,1600, 2600 ms) pCASL. Simulations evaluated the effects of T2 decay and label arrival during the readout. RESULTS: T2 estimates were comparable at PLDs of 1600 and 2600 ms. At the shortest PLD of 600 ms, multi-echo yielded lower T2. Multi-echo demonstrated higher temporal and spatial SNR, whereas T2-prep showed increased T2 blurring and image artifacts in the unsubtracted images, consistent with simulations. CONCLUSION: Although multi-echo provides superior SNR, it may underestimate T2 at short PLDs. The underlying cause of this finding remains unresolved; however, preliminary simulations indicate it could result from partial signal crushing of flowing spins by readout gradients. In contrast, the longer readout of the T2-prep approach is more prone to blurring and artifacts. These findings highlight important trade-offs between the two techniques and underscore the need for careful sequence selection in T2-based BBB water exchange studies.

articles.title: Real-Time Correction of Respiration-Induced  B 0   Changes in Oscillating Steady State Imaging (OSSI) fMRI.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Oscillating steady-state imaging (OSSI) is an fMRI acquisition technique that utilizes a novel oscillating steady-state by combining balanced gradients and quadratic RF phase cycle to achieve a higher SNR compared to spoiled GRE. Despite its SNR advantage, OSSI is sensitive to fluctuations in the  B 0   field due to respiration and drift, which limits the achievable SNR gains. These fluctuations cause shifts in the resonant frequency, disrupting the magnetic steady-state and the functional contrasts. This study proposes a robust zeroth-order prospective correction for multi-shot OSSI fMRI. METHODS: FIDNavs were inserted into a 2D OSSI sequence for real-time processing to track respiration- and drift-induced  B 0   fluctuations during both low-resolution (3-shot) and high-resolution (6-shot) acquisitions. These fluctuations were estimated on a per-shot basis while accounting for shot-dependent phase variations introduced by eddy currents. The resulting  B 0   estimates were then used to dynamically adjust the excitation and receiver phase progressions. RESULTS: Real-time tracking and correction led to substantial improvements in functional sensitivity and signal stability under both regular and deep breathing conditions. In the 3-shot acquisition, tSNR increased by up to 46.8% and activation volume by up to 411.1%, while the 6-shot acquisition exhibited more modest but consistent gains, with tSNR increases of up to 17.2%. Voxel-level time series demonstrated marked suppression of respiration-related oscillations, revealing more stable task-related modulation. CONCLUSION: This approach is effective in reducing  B 0   -induced signal changes, allowing realization of theoretical SNR gains in complex steady-state MRI sequences, particularly in cases affected by respiratory motion.

articles.title: Association Between Myocardial BOLD Reactivity and Peripheral Microvascular Function Assessed by Flow-Mediated Skin Fluorescence.
articles.abstract: Cardiac blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) MRI during breath-hold provides a contrast-free myocardial-specific readout of vasoreactivity. We tested whether myocardial BOLD reactivity covaries with peripheral microvascular function measured by flow-mediated skin fluorescence (FMSF), thereby assessing concordance between two physiologically distinct vascular beds. Twenty-eight participants underwent a mid-diastolic cardiac BOLD MRI at 1.5 T during end-expiratory breath-hold, alongside forearm FMSF during transient brachial artery occlusion. Participants were classified as having FMSF-normal reactivity (NR) or FMSF-abnormal reactivity (AR) based on predefined FMSF criteria (i.e., one or more of the following: reactive hyperemia response [RHR] < 30% or hypoxia sensitivity [HS] < 25). Heartbeat-to-heartbeat myocardial T2 and T2* slopes (ms/hb) and absolute changes (ΔT2, ΔT2*) were compared between cohorts and correlated with FMSF parameters. Compared with AR, the NR showed greater T2 slope (0.1 ± 0.2 vs. -0.2 ± 0.3 ms/hb; p = 0.002), T2* slope (0.1 ± 0.2 vs. 0.0 ± 0.1 ms/hb; p = 0.016), ΔT2 (1.3 ± 2.2 vs. -1.9 ± 2.9 ms; p = 0.003) and ΔT2* (2.4 ± 2.8 vs. -0.1 ± 2.1 ms; p = 0.013). After Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction across 44 correlations, IR index correlated with T2 slope (r = 0.58, q = 0.050), IR max correlated with T2 slope (r = 0.57, q = 0.050), and HS correlated with ΔT2* (r = 0.53, q = 0.050). Interreader reproducibility was good for myocardial BOLD-derived slopes and ΔT2* (ICC = 0.80-0.86) and moderate for ΔT2 (ICC = 0.66). Within this long-COVID cohort, myocardial BOLD reactivity covaried with peripheral microvascular reactivity at the group level. Cardiac BOLD MRI may serve as a myocardial-specific probe of microvascular function within a broader systemic vascular phenotype.

articles.title: Clinical utility of MOLLI T1 mapping using averaged in- and out-of-phase echo times (AIOP) for quantitative assessment of hepatic fibrosis in steatotic livers.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To determine the clinical applicability and robustness of modified Look-Locker inversion recovery (MOLLI) T1 mapping using an averaged in- and out-of-phase echo time (AIOP, TE = 1.8 ms) sequence in patients with varied degrees of hepatic steatosis, comparing its performance with out-of-phase (OP, TE = 1.3 ms) and in-phase (IP, TE = 2.4 ms) MOLLI sequences for noninvasive assessment of liver fibrosis. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 122 patients referred for liver MRI, including three MOLLI T1 mappings (OP, IP, AIOP) and six-point Dixon proton density fat fraction (PDFF) mapping. Regions of interest were placed in homogeneous liver parenchyma. Differences between AIOP and OP or IP T1 values were correlated with PDFF. Patients were stratified by PDFF: <5%, 5-10%, ≥10%. Associations between sequence-specific T1 values and FIB-4 scores were analyzed via Spearman correlation; Friedman tests assessed differences among sequences. RESULTS: Mean T1 was 747.8±97.9 ms (OP), 721.9±88.7 ms (AIOP), and 702.4±84.1 ms (IP) (all pairwise p<0.001). Differences ΔT1OP-AIOP and ΔT1AIOP-IP correlated moderately with PDFF (r=0.660 and 0.544; p<0.001). In highly steatotic livers (PDFF≥10%, n = 16), AIOP T1 demonstrated the strongest correlation with FIB-4 (r=0.621; p=0.010), outperforming OP (r=0.530; p=0.035) and IP (r=0.492; p=0.053) sequences. CONCLUSION: AIOP MOLLI T1 mapping (TE = 1.8 ms) minimizes fat-induced bias inherent in OP and IP acquisitions and shows superior correlation with serologic fibrosis indices in patients with hepatic steatosis levels exceeding 10%. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: AIOP T1 mapping may reduce the influence of steatosis on T1 measurements and may provide values that correlate with serologic fibrosis markers.

articles.title: Multiparametric MRI Tumor Habitat Analysis for Differentiating Non-Enhancing IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma from Low-Grade Glioma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether voxel-wise multiparametric physiologic MRI-based tumor habitat analysis captures intratumoral heterogeneity that differentiates non-enhancing glioblastoma (GBM) from low-grade glioma (LGG) beyond clinical and conventional imaging features. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 84 patients with non-enhancing gliomas (42 GBM, 42 LGG) from November 2007 to October 2024. An external validation cohort from Institution 2 (n = 14; 8 GBM, 6 LGG) was also included. Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), relative cerebral blood volume (rCBV), and volume transfer constant (Ktrans) maps were used to construct voxel-wise habitat clustering via k-means and to extract the 10th and 90th percentiles, mean, and median values. Statistical analyses comprised survival analyses, logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: Voxel-wise clustering delineated six distinct spatial habitats. GBMs were enriched in hypercellular, hypervascular, high-permeability habitats, whereas LGGs predominantly occupied hypocellular, hypovascular, low-permeability habitats. Stratification based on the proportion of high-risk habitat clusters revealed significantly shorter progression-free survival in patients with higher cluster burden (P <.05). The multiparametric model combining ADC, rCBV, and Ktrans achieved the highest AUC (0.83) for differentiating non-enhancing GBM from LGG, compared with 0.59-0.71 for demographic and VASARI-based comparator models. CONCLUSIONS: Multiparametric MRI-based voxel-wise habitat analysis enables accurate, noninvasive differentiation of non-enhancing glioblastoma from low-grade glioma while demonstrating potential prognostic relevance based on intratumoral physiologic heterogeneity. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This study presents a novel voxel-wise multiparametric MRI habitat analysis integrating diffusion, perfusion, and permeability to capture intratumoral heterogeneity in non-enhancing gliomas, thereby improving diagnostic differentiation and potential prognostic assessment beyond conventional imaging methods.

articles.title: Performance of a self-supervised pretrained neural network for orthopedic radiograph classification.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether domain-adaptive self-supervised pretraining of a convolutional neural network on musculoskeletal radiographs improves binary fracture classification and attribution faithfulness relative to ImageNet-pretrained baselines. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study (conducted June 2025 to May 2026) compared three initializations of a ResNet-50 convolutional neural network: supervised ImageNet (control), self-supervised ImageNet (DINO), and DINO further pretrained on 44,029 musculoskeletal radiographs (DINO-Ortho). Each was fine-tuned in three experiments: in-distribution (MURA and FracAtlas), out-of-distribution (5365 external calcaneal radiographs from 1775 patients acquired during 2015-2022), and initial weights (calcaneal fine-tuning). Attribution faithfulness was quantified using Remove and Debias (ROAD) scores from Grad-CAM saliency maps, with higher scores indicating greater faithfulness. AUROCs were compared using DeLong tests, and ROAD scores using Friedman tests with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc pairwise comparisons. RESULTS: DINO-Ortho AUROC did not differ significantly from either baseline in any experiment (0.82 [95% confidence interval, 0.79-0.84] in-distribution and 0.95 [0.93-0.96] with initial weights). DINO-Ortho ROAD scores were significantly higher than both baselines in-distribution (20.01 vs 3.70 and 9.35, respectively) and with initial weights (20.41 vs 12.15 and 1.67, respectively, P < 0.001 for all) and higher than control but not DINO out-of-distribution (15.47 vs 3.06 and 16.09, respectively). All models discriminated poorly out-of-distribution (AUROC 0.65 [0.63-0.67], 0.64 [0.63-0.66], and 0.64 [0.63-0.66] for control, DINO, and DINO-Ortho, respectively). CONCLUSION: With no significant difference in AUROC from either baseline, domain-adapted self-supervised pretraining yielded more faithful attributions than supervised ImageNet pretraining in every experiment and than self-supervised ImageNet pretraining in two of three. No model generalized adequately to unfamiliar anatomy without fine-tuning. Groups fine-tuning on their own musculoskeletal data should therefore consider domain-adapted weights, whose saliency maps more reliably show what drove each prediction, making reliance on irrelevant features easier to detect.

articles.title: FDA Approval of 18F-FET: A Call to Action for Improving Access to Amino Acid PET in the U.S.
Cross-dataset structural brain MRI quality assessment with a 25,857 parameter CNN: Capacity is not the limiting factor.
articles.abstract: Automated quality control of structural brain MRI is needed for reliable large-scale neuroimaging, yet most reported systems are validated only within the dataset used to develop them, and the contribution of non-image factors is rarely quantified. A lightweight CNN with 25,857 parameters was trained on 789 ABIDE subjects (48 quality-fail, prevalence 6.1%) labelled by two-rater consensus, under five-fold stratified group cross-validation repeated ten times, then applied without adaptation to 327 scans from MR-ART, an independent dataset with physically induced head motion. Four ImageNet-pretrained architectures (0.94-23.6 M parameters), four classifiers built on established quality metrics, and a site-identity-only control were evaluated under the same protocol. The lightweight CNN reached AUROC 0.898 ± 0.050 in-domain, matching the strongest metric-based classifier (paired difference 0.032, 95% CI -0.024 to +0.095), and 0.897 (0.863-0.929) under zero-shot transfer - within 0.046 AUROC of a 23.6 M-parameter ResNet-50 at 1/912th the parameters. Three findings bound these results. Site identity alone predicted ABIDE quality labels at AUROC 0.848, though within site the lightweight CNN retained 0.826 against 0.500 for that control. Leave-one-site-out performance fell to 0.791, with specificity 0.989 at seven unseen scanners. Agreement between the two ABIDE raters was slight (Cohen's kappa 0.21), and 20.9% of rated scans were discarded for disagreement. A network of 25,857 parameters is therefore sufficient for cross-dataset brain MRI quality control. On multi-site data the limiting factors are label reliability and site confounding rather than model capacity; we suggest reporting a site-only baseline and an inter-rater agreement statistic as routine.

articles.title: CedeDiff: Context-aware and texture-guided diffusion model for low-dose CT denoising.
articles.abstract: Low-dose CT (LDCT) significantly reduces patient radiation exposure but introduces substantial noise and artifacts. LDCT denoising aims to achieve image quality matching normal-dose CT (NDCT). Although deep learning methods have achieved promising results in LDCT denoising, they often suffer from over-smoothing and loss of fine structural details. Diffusion models have emerged as a powerful class of generative models, demonstrating a remarkable ability to capture complex data distributions and generate high-quality images. In this paper, we propose a contextual edge-enhanced diffusion model (CedeDiff) for LDCT denoising. First, we introduce a stochastic perturbation strategy into the degradation operator. Compared with conventional deterministic degradation, the proposed stochastic degradation strategy better captures the complexity and variability of noise patterns in LDCT images. This design makes the simulated degradation more realistic during training and improves the robustness and generalization of the model. Second, we propose a texture-conditioned diffusion model that allows the denoising network to exploit texture and structural information to guide restoration. Third, to further strengthen guidance during sampling, we introduce disentangled classifier-free guidance, which amplifies the influence of the conditional priors and yields more accurate restoration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art LDCT denoising methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality, with superior noise suppression and detail preservation.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) as a bridge: can ChatGPT-4 help patients understand breast radiology reports?
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess whether ChatGPT-4 improves readability of breast radiology reports by generating simplified summaries and patient-centered recommendations. METHODS: Seventy-five BI-RADS 3, 4, and 5 breast imaging reports were entered into ChatGPT-4 using two prompts: (1) "Please put the report into layperson terms" and (2) "Please provide recommendations for the patient." Readability of original reports and AI-generated outputs was assessed using validated readability metrics, including the Flesch Reading Ease score, Gunning Fog Index, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Coleman-Liau Index, and SMOG Index. Two breast radiologists independently reviewed the AI-generated layperson summaries and recommendations for medical accuracy. Statistical analysis was performed using two-sided, unpaired, equal-variance t-tests. RESULTS: ChatGPT-4-generated layperson summaries demonstrated significantly improved readability compared with the original reports across BI-RADS 3, 4, and 5 categories (all p < 0.05). ChatGPT-4-generated patient recommendations also demonstrated significantly improved readability for BI-RADS 3 reports. For BI-RADS 4 reports, readability improved across several readability metrics with significance observed for a subset of metrics. In contrast, for BI-RADS 5 reports, ChatGPT-4-generated recommendations were less readable than the original reports on several readability metrics. Despite these differences in readability, all AI-generated summaries and recommendations were deemed medically accurate by two breast radiologists. CONCLUSION: ChatGPT-4 generates medically accurate, patient-friendly summaries of BI-RADS 3-5 breast imaging reports with improved readability and may serve as a useful tool for enhancing patient understanding of breast imaging results. However, ChatGPT-4-generated patient recommendations demonstrated variable readability with reduced readable for BI-RADS 5 reports, highlighting the need for further refinement before clinical implementation.
